items.statement: Management will not provide any guidance to stay focused on long-term objectives and avoid distraction
items.quote: One of the things that we have been mentioning is that we would like to desist from providing any guidance of any form as it is providing a distraction from our long-term objective.

items.statement: NIMs have been stable in 3.4%-3.5% range with increasing bias since merger
items.quote: For example, the NIMs have been in the range of 3.4% to 3.5% with an increasing bias.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio stable at 40%-41% with decreasing bias since merger
items.quote: The cost-to-income has been in the range of 40% to 41% with a decreasing bias.

items.statement: Medium to long-term glide path to bring cost-to-income down to 30% remains intact
items.quote: On cost to income, yes, in the medium to long term, that is the glide path that I have, and I'm reasonably sanguine that we will do.

items.statement: Bank remains disciplined on deposit pricing, not competing on rates
items.quote: We have tried to remain disciplined on price as much as possible to win over the customer through engagement and service delivery. So we've not gone into this term -- in terms of the rate as such.

items.statement: Consciously losing transactional corporate business that doesn't meet pricing thresholds to adjust mix
items.quote: What we are losing is transactional business consciously because it's not meeting our pricing thresholds. We are all right to do so because we -- maybe this is the best time for us to adjust our mix.

items.statement: Loan-deposit ratio to be brought down faster than anticipated for profitable growth
items.quote: It is in our interest to bring down the loan-deposit ratios much faster than what one would have anticipated. It is in our interest, and I'll explain that to you probably when one of you ask questions.

items.statement: No compromise on strategic investments in distribution and technology despite cost pressures
items.quote: I'm very clear about it. So what we are trying to do is how do we juice out efficiencies out of digitization, out of better productivity.

items.statement: Added 2.2 million new customer relationships in Q1 FY25, similar to previous quarter
items.quote: We did add 2.2 million new customer relationships in the quarter. So last quarter was very similar.

items.statement: HDFC Limited non-retail deposits of Rs 160 billion ran down in Q1 FY25
items.quote: At least Rs.160 billion of an erstwhile HDFC non-retail deposits, which ran down, has given us a very tepid kind of a net attrition on a period-end basis.

items.statement: Borrowings reduced by close to Rs 600 billion in Q1 FY25, including Rs 150 billion commercial paper maturity
items.quote: In the quarter, we did take down close to INR60,000-odd crores or INR600 billion of borrowings down. About INR150 billion was commercial papers - which matured, and we had to run it down anyway.

items.statement: Scheduled borrowing maturity for FY25 is Rs 650 billion, with Rs 250 billion maturing in Q1
items.quote: For the year, I think the maturity profile is about INR650 billion for the year. That is scheduled maturity, INR600 billion for the year, out of which maybe INR250 billion were maturing that got paid in June quarter.

items.statement: EPS remained stable at Rs 21.3 in Q1 FY25 vs Rs 21.4 pre-merger
items.quote: The EPS for the bank, June, pre-merger was 21.4 - last year June. And in this quarter, it was 21.3. So thereabouts, right, it is similar levels.

items.statement: PSL compliance focus on small and marginal farmer category with dual qualification for weaker sections
items.quote: Our focus, if you think about PSL for us, which we've always said is that our focus is how do we get as much as possible the small and marginal farmer and with the dual qualification for weaker.

items.statement: Repo-linked loans: 70% of mortgages and 40% of non-mortgages are external benchmark linked
items.quote: Mortgages is about for total 30, 70 or so, 30 fixed and 70 is external. Mortgages will have about 27, non-mortgages is about 40, which is external, EBLR linked.

items.statement: Expect FY25 volume growth in replacement segment to remain healthy and OEM growth in most categories led by 2-wheelers, passenger and MHCV to continue to be good
items.quote: We expect FY '25 volume growth in replacement segment to remain healthy and OEM growth in most categories, led by 2-wheelers and passengers and MHCV will continue to be good.

items.statement: Raw material cost increased approximately 5% quarter-on-quarter, singularly responsible for gross margin contraction
items.quote: Our raw material cost has gone up approximately by 5% quarter -on-quarter and this is singularly responsible for the contraction in gross margin.

items.statement: Domestic natural rubber prices surged 25-30% over past few months, currently at INR200/kg, highest in 13 years
items.quote: Domestic natural rubber prices has surged by about 25% to 30% over the past few months. And currently, it has scaled INR200 which is the highest in the last 13 years.

items.statement: Price hikes taken: commercial segment 2.3% including July, passenger segment 2.5-3% including July, 2-wheelers 1%, OEM indexed with 2% indexation benefit in Q2
items.quote: We have tried to mitigate it with price increase in all segments, led by replacement in commercial segment, as we speak, including July, we have had a 2.3% price hike. In passenger segment, including July, we have had a similar price hike of around 2.5% to 3%.

items.statement: Need 3-4% overall price increase progressively to recover cost gaps from Q1 and current quarter
items.quote: I think progressively because raw material costs impacts as we based on arrivals. I think about overall to recover all the cost gaps in quarter 1 and now, 3% to 4% kind of increase would be required progressively.

items.statement: Indicated capex for the year at around INR1,000 crores, INR254 crores spent in Q1, all expansion projects progressing as per plan
items.quote: We indicated a capex for the year at around INR1,000 crores, out of which about INR254 crores were spent in quarter 1, and all expansion projects are progressing as per plan.

items.statement: International order base looks strong, growth coming from focused markets of Latin America, Europe and progressively US, double-digit growth expected to continue through the year
items.quote: Our order base looks strong and the growth is coming from desired focused markets of Latin America, Europe and progressively, it will also come from US.

items.statement: Rural demand coming back gradually, with good monsoons expect rural demand to keep coming back sustainably at high level compared to urban demand
items.quote: Rural demand seems to be coming back gradually. With good monsoons, we expect rural demand to keep coming back as sustainably as a high level as compared to urban demand.

items.statement: International business saliency at 20% in Q1, targeted at 25% in 2-3 years, margin accretive, launched 42+ off-highway SKUs and 30+ passenger vehicle SKUs in Q1 for international markets
items.quote: International business has been a focus. 20% is saliency in quarter 1, and we have targeted at levels of 25% in 2 to 3 years. This is margin accretive.

items.statement: Consolidated position in EV OEMs with close to 30% share in 2-wheeler, 3-wheeler EV OEMs and 4-wheeler EVs sold by OEMs in India, expect breakthrough in international OEMs in next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: We have consolidat ed our position in electric vehicle OEMs in both 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler. We have close to 30% share now in both 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler EV OEMs as well as in 4 -wheeler EVs being sold by OEMs in India.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 12.2% in Q1, contraction of 130 bps QoQ primarily due to raw material price increase and higher planned marketing expense
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR388.2 crores, this is about 12.2% margin. This is a contraction of 130 basis points quarter-on-quarterand primarily, the contraction is on account of increase in raw material prices and higher but planned marketing expense in quarter 1.

items.statement: Gross margin shrunk 184 bps YoY and 306 bps QoQ largely due to increase in raw material costs, natural rubber prices at INR207/kg highest in 12 years
items.quote: Coming to gross margin , our gross margin during the quarter shrunk by about 184 basis points year -on-year and 306 basis points quarter -on-quarter, largely due to increase in raw material costs that you know about 5% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Significant freight hikes 3x-4x in international business coupled with container non-availability, headwind expected to continue in July and part of August
items.quote: There have been some headwinds in terms of significant freight hikes to the extent of 3x to 4x in international business and also, coupled with this was the issue of non -availability of containers.

items.statement: Marketing spend increased 100 bps over last year average spend in Q1 for brand repositioning, invested heavily in IPL, World Cup, election week and GEC properties
items.quote: We have invested heavily in brand repositioning in quarter 1 to the extent off 100 bps over last year average spend on marketing front.

items.statement: Full-year volume guidance of 6.5 million tonnes cement, excluding clinker sales
items.quote: I think we are reasonably sure that we should be very close to 6.5 million. This includes the lower vol umes that have been moved, and this definitely excludes the clinker sale. So, 6.5 million is our volume guidance

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA guidance of ₹350-375 crore, translating to ₹550-575 per tonne
items.quote: From a profitability guidance perspective, we believe that t he overall EBITDA should be in the range of around ₹350 crores to ₹375 crores, which should roughly translate to ₹550 to ₹575 EBITDA per tonne

items.statement: Prices dropped ₹10/bag from Q4 to end of Q1, and a further ₹5/bag from end of Q1 to mid-July
items.quote: We believe, or at least what we have noticed in most of our operating markets, there has been a drop of ₹5 per bag from the exit of Q4 till middle of t his month. That has been the case across the markets

items.statement: Expect seasonal price increase of ₹10-15/bag from mid-Q3 as demand picks up
items.quote: We are not trying to be euphoric about the potential kind of a price increase that is possible in the marketplace, what we have penci lled is ₹10 to ₹15 per bag potentially to go up from middle of Q3 is what we are factoring, which is normal seasonal kind of thing

items.statement: Demand expected to pick up sharply from mid-Q3 as election-related deferrals resume and Amaravati project progresses
items.quote: we strongly believe that from middle of Q3, the demand is likely to sh arp up more sharply

items.statement: FY25 capex plan of ~₹300 crore, with ₹33 crore spent in Q1; Andhra Cements expansion ₹255 crore this year, balance in FY26
items.quote: If you look at the Slide 12, we did indicate the overall kind of a CapEx plan for Andhra, it is ₹255 for the current financial year, balance in FY '26.

items.statement: Targeting ₹250/tonne cost reduction at clinker level from Andhra Cements efficiency capex, plus ₹25/tonne at cement grinding level
items.quote: So all in all, we are looking at close to ₹250 per tonne, up to clinker to come down. And from a perspective of cement grinding, we expect the number of units to come down by five units. So that should be another ₹25-odd at the cement level.

items.statement: Clinker sales of ~84,000 tonnes in Q1 at ₹3,050/tonne ex-works due to excess inventory; not a regular strategy
items.quote: Yeah, I think it's around 84,000 has been the sale of clinker for the last quarter. The average realisation is close to around ₹3,050 kind of a number per tonne. I'm talking about ex-work.

items.statement: Industry utilisation in AP/Telangana at 45-50%; new supply ramp-ups (Shree, Dalmia, My Home, UltraTech, Deccan) to be absorbed by demand recovery from mid-Q3
items.quote: So the average capacity utilisation in our view is somewhere around 45% to 50% in general. There could be one or two units, which could be exceptionally higher or lower than this, but in general, the capacity utilisation is somewhere around in the range of around 45% to 50%.

items.statement: Net debt target capped at ₹1,250-1,300 crore for FY25; gross debt not to exceed current level; Vizag land sale not factored into cash flows this year
items.quote: I think we should be at a similar level. I think around ₹1,300 odd, ₹1,250 to ₹1,300 is what we are limiting ourselves. So I think we would be capping our net debt position there. Gross, we would not exceed the current position itself.

items.statement: Andhra Cements expected to break even by Q1 FY26 as ramp-up and optimisation progress
items.quote: Yeah, I think we shoul d be very close to that time line . It's just a question of ramping up. The internal capacity as well as optimi sation is progressing. It's a question of doing volumes. I think we should be breakevening by Q1 is what we strongly think

items.statement: Renewable energy roadmap: 6MW solar each at Gudipadu and Dachepalli in FY25; 4MW WHR at Gudipadu by FY27; 4MW solar at Mattampally and Jeerabad by FY27; 2MW WHR at Mattampally by FY28; 9MW WHR at Dachepalli by FY29
items.quote: If you can look at the same Slide 12, yeah, we did indicate just solar Gudipadu is 6 MW by FY '25, waste heat recovery for Gudipadu by FY '27. Solar 4 megawatt at M attampally by FY '27. Waste heat recovery for Line 1 at Mattampally, which is 2 MW by FY '28. Solar at Jeerabad 4 megawatt by FY

items.statement: Madhya Pradesh market down 15% YoY in Q1; Gujarat down 5% YoY; Odisha flat to slightly positive
items.quote: assessment is that Madhya Pradesh market has come down by 15% year -on-year. Whereas Gujarat actually is trending upward, but it is 5% lower at the current quarter year-on-year kind of thing. Odisha is flat to slightly with a positive bias

items.statement: Green power share at 30% currently; moving to 50% could add ₹50-75/tonne EBITDA as blended power cost falls from ₹6 to ₹4.75-5/unit
items.quote: Now the minut e we go up to 50%. That is incrementally. We believe that it should contribute close to around another ₹50 to ₹75 per tonne because it also has its cost, right? It's not that it is coming free

items.statement: Hyderabad prices already at floor; further significant decline unlikely as industry bleeding; Chennai prices at par or below Hyderabad for first time
items.quote: For the first time in my career, I've seen Chennai prices, either at par or lower than par, this we have never noticed. So would Hyderabad prices get corrected way below Chennai prices just because Chennai prices have come down? Only time will tell. But I think Hyderabad prices are not at its best either.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of ₹150-200/tonne/year for pyro section plus ~₹100/tonne for other consumables; long-term kiln overhauls capitalised
items.quote: But all in all, what we generally do not only for the kiln, but the entire equipment, anywhere between ₹150 to ₹200 per tonne as we replace the maintenance kind of a cost for the overall kind of maintenance.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth uptick starting Q2 FY25
items.quote: We do believe from Q2 you will see us back on the growth side and we will build on that as we accelerate towards where we want to go with our clients.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA for FY25 to exceed last year's 11% consolidated level
items.quote: Our goal remains to achieve double-digit EBITDA. We believe we will be much higher than last year's 11% on a consolidated level.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 9.9%, up 176 bps QoQ
items.quote: On the EBITDA level, we grew 21% quarter-on-quarter, ending at a 9.9% margin. It's a bit short, but still a growth of 176 bps points.

items.statement: Strong demand across US and Europe; opening Toronto office to service North America
items.quote: We have never had this kind of demand from our customers, especially in U.S. and Europe. And I think that number is only going to increase is what I see as we keep hiring more account delivery managers and account sales managers for the clients that we already serve.

items.statement: Targeting 70% revenue from outside India (currently 50%)
items.quote: I believe the right sweet spot for us is 70% of the revenue should come from outside India. That's always been the dream and that's where all our investments has been and that gives us a good balance from a risk perspective as well over the next few.

items.statement: Investing in labs, centers of excellence, delivery teams across three verticals and horizontals
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust. For the first time, we crossed Rs 100 crore in cash on hand as of June 2024, and this number will keep improving as we continue to build a strong business model with investmen ts in labs, centers of excellence, and delivery teams across the three verticals and horizontals

items.statement: Execution risk from visa/work permit delays for onsite hiring in US, UK, Germany, Canada
items.quote: For execution, I do need a lot of visas, whether it's UK, Canada, Germany, U.S., and that's something Onward does not have. That's a new business for us in the last three years. So, we are building on that and we are seeing amazing momentum towards that.

items.statement: Signed Rs 6.5 crore 3-year deal with Microsoft including Copilot GenAI licenses
items.quote: Just to give you a perspective, a couple of days back, we signed a Rs 6.5 crore deal with Microsoft for the next three years or something along those lines. We see that we are confident of the demand that we see for the next three years.

items.statement: Annual rate negotiations with T&M clients (80-90% of revenue) showing positive outcomes
items.quote: And on the pricing side, it's always a conversation because the majority of our business model, 80% or 90% of our revenue comes from time and material. So, every year, Sapna, my team and me have a conversation with all our clients, not just the top 5 clients, every client that we have on the T&M side, which is on pricing, right? And we see a lot of positives.

items.statement: Targeting 200-300 H-1B visas within 2-3 years to drive substantial revenue growth
items.quote: For example, we applied for over 200 H-1Bs last year and received 25 to 30 approvals—our first approvals in six to seven years. This is a significant development, and we aim to have 200 to 300 H-1Bs available within 2-3 years, which we anticipate will drive substantial revenue growth.

items.statement: Net headcount target of 2,700-2,900 consolidated; focus on adding 1,500 people in Europe and US
items.quote: I think it will be between 2,700 and 2,900 people net as a consolidated basis. And what is important is can we add that 1,500 people in Europe and U.S.?

items.statement: Q1 revenue shortfall due to lack of technical people in US and work permit delays in Europe
items.quote: Yes, so two things from a U.S. perspective, we did not have the technical people and that's something where we lost some traction, let's say, in the month of June. And from a Europe perspective, the projects that we won, which were supposed to start billing in Q4, did not start and some are starting as I said as early as coming Monday. Because work permits took longer and something or the other.

items.statement: Dividend increased from Rs 3 to Rs 5 per share, approved at AGM
items.quote: Earlier today in the AGM, we increased the dividend from Rs. 3 to Rs. 5, which got approved by the shareholders.

items.statement: No demand deferment seen; customers want immediate project starts after award
items.quote: No. So, another point that you mentioned, execution challenge continues to be there for us in Europe and U.S., where after winning a project, and I have shared it before as well, customer wants to start tomorrow because every company that we are working with, and you guys all know some of the names, are very cash-rich, very powerful, very largest companies in the world, and they have huge budgets.

items.statement: Reducing customer count from 85 to target 60-75 for deeper engagements across three horizontals
items.quote: In terms of customer engagements, we had about 250 customers three years ago. Now, we are down to 85 plus customers, aiming for a sweet spot of 60 to 75 customers to build deeper engagements and add value across our three horizontals: mechanica l engineering, embedded electronics, and digital services

items.statement: Do not share quarterly or annual revenue projections; too young as a company
items.quote: We don't share projections. As I said we are too young. We have to get to what we are good at and get back to work.

items.statement: Deposits grew 8.5% YoY and advances 11.5% YoY, within guidance range of 9-11% for deposits and 11-13% for advances for FY25
items.quote: The deposits have grown by 8.5% YoY, advances by 11.5%, largely in alignment with our guidance range of 9 % to 11% for deposits and 11% to 13% for advances.

items.statement: NIM at 3.05% surpasses guidance of 2.8% to 3% for FY25
items.quote: Our NIM is at 3.05% surpassing our guidance of 2.8% to 3% for FY25.

items.statement: Gross NPA reduced to 4.54% in line with guidance, with gross recovery of Rs 3,368 crores and slippages restricted to Rs 2,318 crores
items.quote: In line with our guidance, gross NPA reduced to 4.54% with gross recovery at 3,368 crores and slippages restricted to 2,318 crores.

items.statement: Board approved capital raise of Rs 10,000 crores for FY25, comprising Rs 6,000 crores equity and Rs 4,000 crores through AT1 and Tier 2 instruments
items.quote: We also have a plan to raise capital to the extent of Rs.10,000 crores for FY25. It has been approved by the board, of which Rs.6,000 crores will be equity and Rs.4,000 crores through AT 1 and Tier 2 instruments.

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduced by 5 bps QoQ due to sufficient liquidity; may increase rates going forward to fund advance growth
items.quote: QoQ, the cost of deposits is slightly reduced by 5 bps over March '24. It is because we did not take much funds in the market and we have got enough of liquidity with us.

items.statement: Yield on advances declined ~11 bps QoQ primarily due to lower dummy ledger recovery (Rs 607 cr vs Rs 850 cr prior quarter) and only 25 bps MCLR reset passed on
items.quote: Yield on advances has declined by about 15 days, primarily due to the fall in our DL recovery. About 11 bps impact it had because of the DL recovery compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: Standard asset provisioning of Rs 1,296 crores made for anticipated distress in a couple of accounts; described as one-off, not expected next quarter
items.quote: Standard asset provisioning, we have done to the extent of about Rs.1,296 crores. It's increased to that extent. This increase is due to an anticipated distress or potential restructuring in a couple of accounts.

items.statement: Digital frauds constitute 70-80% of reported frauds (Rs 341 cr outstanding); Bank has implemented real-time monitoring, AI, velocity checks and 24/7 cyber security center
items.quote: So, almost like 70% to 80% of these frauds are digital frauds of small in nature and of course the remaining are credit and credit fraud that is happening.

items.statement: Agriculture book growing consistently at 21-22% YoY; gold loans up from Rs 43,000 cr to Rs 66,000 cr in agri; SHG lending growing 30% with low delinquency
items.quote: We would be growing consistently. We have been growing at 21% or 22% in my agri book. So, it will be increasing in the same level.

items.statement: RAM advances grew 14.5% YoY vs large corporate 7.8%; NBFC book at Rs 1,20,065 cr (99% rated A and above); excess liquidity ~Rs 65,000 cr
items.quote: We grew better under RAM advances by 14.5%, while large corporate advances grew by 7.8%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected in 44% to 45.5% range for FY25; ROA guided above 1% (achieved 1.06% in Q1)
items.quote: Cost to income ratio, we are in the 44% range, 44.08%. So, in terms of guidance for cost to income ratio, where we not formally given out any guidance, we expect to be in the range of about 45% to 45.5% somewhere there.

items.statement: Credit cost guided below 1% for FY25 (73 bps in Q1); Bank expects to maintain this despite Q1 standard asset provisioning
items.quote: Our credit cost is 73 basis points. We look at it from a standard advances point of view. So, that is what we are looking at in terms of guiding. So, we would look at keeping a control on that unless there's any one-off event but that is what we're guiding in terms of keeping it below 1%.

items.statement: Plan to open 200-250 branches in FY25, primarily premium branches at RUSU locations; rationalized 25 branches last year
items.quote: This year we would be opening about 200-250 branches. And basically, these branches will be in the premium kind of a branches.

items.statement: ECL implementation expected FY26-27; gap with current norms narrowed significantly; no substantial balance sheet impact anticipated; capital raise not linked to ECL
items.quote: We will be able to absorb the impact condition of the ECL and I know the timelines will be given for one year timeline to implement the ECL norms after the final guidelines and the news is that it will be implemented for FY26-27.

items.statement: PSLC income Rs 955 cr in Q1 (typically Q1 event); traded at Rs 1.80-2.00; buyers mainly private sector banks with shortfall
items.quote: fees, we have got about Rs. 955 crores. That is generally a Q1 event. So, we would not see that recurring in subsequent quarters to this extent

items.statement: Telangana farm loan waiver impact unknown; amounts credited to farmer accounts then to loan accounts; second phase completes by Aug 15; no significant GNPA jump expected
items.quote: It's done usually, the amounts are credited to the farmers account and from there it is credited to the loan account. And it has just started. So, we will not know the impact because we are doing it in two phases. The second phase will be completed by August 15th.

items.statement: Construction commenced at Thervoykandigai; plant and machinery erection in progress, trial by end of calendar year, production from Q4 2025
items.quote: Erection of plant and machinery is in progress and is expected to be completed for trial by the end of this calendar year and production to commence from Q4 2025 at our unit at Thervoykandigai, Tamil Nadu, where we are increasing capacities in Lead vertical from 1,32,000 metric ton to 2,04,000 metric ton per annum in two Phases.

items.statement: Lead production target for FY25 is 85,000 to 90,000 metric tons; FY26 target is 100,000 to 110,000 metric tons
items.quote: The production sales in terms of metric ton should be around -- last year, it was about 71,000. This year, it should be around the range of 85,000 to 90,000 metric tons

items.statement: Expect 15% volume growth in coming years, 20% ROCE growth, EBITDA margins tending towards 7% to 8%, value-added products increasing to 60% plus
items.quote: So we see the trend continue for us. And we have also kind of released our investor presentation where we see the growth numbers in volumes to continue for us. So there will be 15% volume growth in the coming years. In terms of the return on capital employed, we expect 20% growth. And in terms of EBITDA margins, we will be tending towards 7% to 8% levels and we will be increasing our value-added p

items.statement: Sales mix domestic 35%, export 65% expected to remain similar with plus/minus 5% variation
items.quote: The domestic markets for our product portfolio is seeing a positive momentum in growth. In future, we expect the numbers to remain at similar level with a variation of plus or minus 5%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin percentage remains constant at 5% to 6%; absolute EBITDA grows with volume; new project will increase both percentage and absolute EBITDA
items.quote: But EBITDA, we should not see in absolute terms. We should see in the percentage terms. So in terms of percentage, it is remains constant at the level of 5% to 6% EBITDA. Now, over the period, we are increasing the volume. So naturally in absolute terms, overall EBITDA value also going up gradually and once our new project comes in, the Thervoykandigai, EBITDA in terms of percentage and absolute t

items.statement: Pricing arrangement uses previous month average applied to next month providing natural hedging
items.quote: Pricing arrangement is such that previous month average will be applied to the next month. So natural hedging is there.

items.statement: Global lead market growing 6-7% CAGR; India growing 12-13%; strong demand supports capacity expansion to 204,000 tons
items.quote: Globally, lead market is growing at about 6% to 7%. Now, when it comes to India, India is also growing at relatively 12% to 13%. And we see a lot of potential in the global demand. And that is one of the reasons which initiated the expansion plan for the Thervoykandigai unit where we are increasing our capacities from 1,32,000 tons to 204,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Currency exposure mainly USD; hedged via natural hedge and forward contracts per risk management policy; minimal P&L impact
items.quote: So in terms of currency, our major exposure is towards USD, both on the import leg as well as the USD leg. We have defined risk management policies wherein we hedge our currency risk, mostly its natural hedge and balance, we hedge -- do a forward contract and hedge the balance. So generally, for currency fluctuation, there is not much impact in our P&L

items.statement: Multi-sourcing strategy from 70+ countries, 270+ suppliers with long-term contracts ensuring supply consistency
items.quote: So, on the sourcing part, when you mentioned the scrapyards, so we follow a multi-sourcing strategy and right now we are procuring from almost 70 plus countries. And it's very important to note that we have an overall supplier base of 270 plus and most of them have long-term association with our company. And furthermore, it is important to note as well that we have long-term contracts with them. S

items.statement: Smelting capacity to increase from 80,000 to 160,000 metric tons per annum in two phases at Thervoykandigai
items.quote: The existing capacity for smelting is about 80,000 metric ton. And when we make this Thervoykandigai plant operational, this smelting capacity will increase up to 1,60,000 metric tons in two phases. When the two phases get complete, our overall smelting capacity should be around 1,60,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Aluminum die-cast alloy segment paused due to unprofitable market; reviewing portfolio for value-added products or forward integration
items.quote: No. So, aluminum, what is happening is -- I'll just give you a background on aluminum. We were manufacturing the die cast alloy segment, and unfortunately, for the last two years, the particular industry was bleeding. And even though that we had, I mean, initiated production and sold the material, we don't want to enter into a bandwagon effect where we get into a fragmented market and have to rush

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margins targeted at 7% to 7.5% by FY27 from current 5% to 6%
items.quote: Till FY '27 -- yeah, so this will span over the next three years where right now we are doing about 5% to 6% and by -- in the next three years, we will be tending towards 7% to 7.5%.

items.statement: Lead EBITDA margins expected to improve 120-150 bps to 6% to 6.5%
items.quote: we will see a positive impact on the lead margins to the extent of about 120 to 150 basis points. So we see that number come to about 6% to 6.5%.

items.statement: Plastics revenue target of INR50 crores with positive EBITDA this year

items.quote: We have a target of 15 branches this year and we plan to open all these 15 branches in the Tier 2 towns.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance for FY25 is 13% to 14%.
items.quote: No, we are looking at 13% to 14% of credit growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance for FY25 is 11% to 12%.
items.quote: Deposits growth, we are looking at around 11% to 12% of growth.

items.statement: NIM for Q1 FY25 is 3.06%; target is to maintain around 3.10% for FY25.
items.quote: Our NIM for Q1 is at 3.06%. We intend to maintain it at around 3.10%.

items.statement: Borrowings increased need-based to meet surging credit demand and maintain regulatory ratios.
items.quote: since we have to meet our credit requirements and there are certain ratios which are supposed to be main tained as per regulatory prescriptions. So, need-based, wherever we see that some gap is there, some requirement is there, need-based we go to market and do that borrowing, that is need

items.statement: Medium enterprise book grew 74.81% YoY driven by aggressive TReDS platform discounting and low base.
items.quote: Because of that, this 74% growth is visible and major part of that has come from TReDS, apart from normal growth.

items.statement: Contingent liabilities of Rs 8,450 cr (income tax) and Rs 1,146 cr (indirect tax) are disputed; appeals filed with strong indication of favorable outcome; no provision made.
items.quote: In seven to eight cases, we are having a strong indication that our appeal will be considered favorably. So, provision has not been made because we do not foresee any challenge.

items.statement: Farm loan waiver announcements in some states have many conditions; bank has capability to withstand any impact if implemented.
items.quote: unless or until anything comes out on paper in black and white, it will be difficult to comment on that. But having said that, since it ’s phenomena which is going on for last many years, and we have not faced much challenge on that direction. If at all it happens in any of the states, we are having that capability to withstand that

items.statement: Target CD ratio of 75% by maintaining deposit growth 8-10% and advances growth 12-14%
items.quote: We are planning to reach to 75pc by keeping our deposit growth of 8 -10pc and advances rate of 12 -14pc.

items.statement: Slippage ratio target around 1% for FY25
items.quote: our target is to keep it around 1% in this year also so that the dec reasing trend continues

items.statement: IT initiative budget of Rs 1000 crore; Rs 280 crore orders placed; RFPs for SD WAN, APM, FXPC, Omni Channel, Network Refresh, Overseas Finacle Upgradation, Security Upgradation to be floated this quarter and next
items.value: IT budget Rs 1000 crore; Rs 280 crore orders placed
items.quote: we had in the previous yearly results we have spoken about the IT initiative budget of Rs.1000 crore and various projects have already been started. Around Rs.280 crores of orders have been placed

items.statement: Tab Banking at 1700 branches, targeting 2000 this quarter and all 3000+ branches by year end
items.value: 1700 branches now, target 2000 this quarter, 3000+ by year end
items.quote: Bank started Tab Banking previously and now we have around 1700 branches which are already having Tab and we propose to take to 2000 this quarter and by the year end we intend to reach to all 3000 plus branches.

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved 26 bps YoY to 3.29%; Global NIM improved 23 bps YoY to 3.09%
items.quote: Domestic NIM improved by 26 bps to 3.29% on a YoY basis. Our Global NIM improved by 23 bps to 3.09% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduced 12 bps over last six months from 4.91% to 4.79%
items.quote: Our Cost of Deposit has come down over the last six months . In December'23 it was 4.91, now it is 4.79. It's a 12 bps reduction in cost of deposit.

items.statement: CASA share improved 52 bps YoY to 38.62%; focus on CASA and retail term deposits, reducing bulk deposit dependence
items.quote: Our CASA share improved by 52 bps to 38.62%.

items.statement: Written-off book recovery run rate may slow; low-hanging fruit recovered; 19,000 crore in NCLT; special OTS scheme from 1st July to boost recovery
items.quote: Going forward, the run rate for recovery of return of accoun ts may not be at the same level but now we have to more depend upon the field ground level because small accounts are also part of the written off account

items.statement: Board and AGM approved issuance of 400 crore equity shares (face value Rs 4,000 crore); seeking government approval for first tranche of Rs 2,000 crore to reduce govt holding below 75%
items.quote: we have already taken Board approval and our AGM has a lso approved for issuing 400 crore equity shares for the face value of 4,000 crores. And if entire thing is done, then we will be able to reduce our government holding to less than 75

items.statement: Co-lending partnerships with MAS Financial and other NBFCs across MSME, retail, agri; technology stabilized; expect benefits from next quarter
items.quote: our technology partner is well stabilized. And I think now it is more than six months it is stabilized. Earlier, we had taken them on board, there were certain initial hiccups. Now, technology is fully stabilized and we are able to onboard our co - lending customers also on a regular basis

items.statement: Solar/renewable energy scheme launched; expect to build good portfolio in 6-9 months
items.quote: we expect that maybe in 6 to 9 months we will build up a good portfolio under this scheme.

items.statement: Agri loan waiver risk limited; minimal exposure in Telangana and Maharashtra (10% branches in West)
items.quote: Telangana, we don't have much presence in Telangana because our presence in that state is not much and our exposure to the KCC segment is very small.

items.statement: Overseas deposits grew 48% YoY (~Rs 4,000 crore); Funds Committee monitors domestic vs overseas rates daily for cheaper funding
items.quote: our international deposit also, we have grown on a YoY basis by 48%. What we do on a daily basis, our Funds Committee meets and deposit opportunities, we see whether domestically it is cheaper or overseas centres it is cheaper, including our hedging cost.

items.statement: Yield on advances QoQ decline due to one-time interest recovery of ~Rs 100 crore in previous quarter; 81 crore gap caused 26 bps drop
items.quote: yield on advances has come down because in the previous quarter, we had recovered from the TWO where the.....around 100 crores was part of interest income which was ....previous quarter we recovered. So that was the reason that this quarter, the yield on advances has come down by 109cr......28.....so there is a 81 crores gap in the ....so 26 bps is the gap.

items.statement: Treasury profit outlook: no forward guidance; only incremental FVTPL gains going forward; AFS gains go to reserves not P&L
items.quote: we do not speculate and we do not even give any forward guidance also because this is a market based phenomena which we cannot comment upon.

items.statement: Expects Europe business to deliver ~20% CAGR over 5 years and U.S. business ~30% CAGR from FY26 over next 2 years
items.quote: So over a period of 5 years, I expect the Europe business to consistently give us CAGR of close to 20%. U.S., quite frankly, it's all about timing and new approvals and how fast we are able to come out of the slack that we have right now on product supply. But from next year onwards, I feel clearly close to 30% can be expected from U.S.

items.statement: Expects emerging markets to grow 18-20% CAGR for next couple of years
items.quote: I think 18% to 20% is a good expectation to keep from the emerging business for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expects other expenses to stabilize at INR110-120 crores per quarter going forward
items.quote: I cannot directly quantify everything, but I can roughly tell you that you can expect, I think other expenses in total, we'll be able to maintain in the margin of INR110 crores , INR120 crores per quarter going forward.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to normalize from Q3, minimum 15% for full year FY25
items.quote: So by Q3, if I'm going to say 15%, we are still looking at a year where we are barely managing to stay at the 15% level. I can be frank about that. We will be trying very hard to do better than that, but one can expect minimum 15% for the whole year.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR250 crores for FY25 maintained; INR100 crores already invested in Warren Remedies API facility
items.quote: We'll be able to maintain as per commit.

items.statement: No major capex expected after current round; only maintenance capex going forward
items.quote: So once this round of capex is done, we are not expecting any more capex for the company. What we will need is some kind of maintenance capex, which is a routine across sites.

items.statement: European business has a very healthy order book position currently
items.quote: Actually, European business has a very healthy order book position right now.

items.statement: Gross margin decline due to U.S. supply shortfall (~INR20 crores) and shift of profitable toothpaste variants to subsidiary
items.quote: So like I said, the gross margins this quarter are more a function of the business product contribution, kind of composition, because we are short of close to 20 CR in supply to U.S. market, which is second to India, the most profitable business of the company.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin of minimum 15% by Q3 FY25, with Q4 stronger
items.quote: By third quarter, I'm looking at a minimum of 15%, if not more.

items.statement: Domestic anti-infective and respiratory portfolio revival seen in last 10 days of June; expects robust Q2 with timely monsoon
items.quote: Fortunately, the rains are on time this year and looks like a good season for respiratory and antibiotics both. So Q2, I'm expecting for these brands also to start contributing, and that will help us show a very robust performance for India business.

items.statement: Flipping API sales mix from 60% internal/40% external to 40% internal/60% external from this year
items.quote: From this yea r, we are flipping the ratio and expect to be able to sell around 60% of what we manufacture

items.statement: Goa Plant 2 sterile lines remediation to be completed by October; FDA inspection and status clearance needed before full U.S. supply ramp
items.quote: According to me, if I'm not mistaken, by October, we will be completely ready with all lines remediated and running. And after that, we'll be able to give product from the plant at full potential.

items.statement: Expects to borrow incremental INR100 crores beyond cash flows to meet capex commitments
items.quote: I think we will require to borrow close to another INR100 crores to meet with all the commitments we have made for capex.

items.statement: PSL shortfall deposits to reduce below 5% of total assets by FY27
items.quote: And it expects that by FY '27, the same would meaningfully reduce and come down to below 5.0% of our Total Assets.

items.statement: RIDF book to fall below INR 40,000 crores in FY25 and well below 5% of total assets by FY27
items.quote: When we look at FY '25, the RIDF book, which is about INR 44,000 crores on a net basis should already come below INR 40,000 crores.

items.statement: SME and Mid-Corporate advances to grow at mid-20s percentage
items.quote: We do believe that Mid-Corporate and SME will grow at mid-20s percentage.

items.statement: Retail advances growth to be subdued in FY25 at low double-digit to teens, improving in FY26-27
items.quote: I think we get calibrated to more like low -- very low double-digit-to-teens kind of a growth.

items.statement: Core fee income expected to continue growing at 20% plus
items.quote: We are confident that the fee trend should hold up about 20% plus.

items.statement: UPI market share expected to moderate as business distributes among four banks
items.quote: However, it expects some moderation going ahead.

items.statement: Net Interest Margin maintained at 2.4% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The Bank's Net Interest Margin, as I stated earlier, at 2.4% remained steady compared to last quarter.

items.statement: RIDF book reduction to materially aid margins in FY26 and FY27
items.quote: The P&L impact will start materially playing out in FY '26 and '27.

items.statement: Security Receipts carrying value at INR 850 crores, face value INR 3,500 crores, expected to become zero in FY25 without P&L hit
items.quote: The carrying value is of INR 850 crores that we have in the balance sheet today, the face value of these security receipts is about INR 3,500 crores.

items.statement: Unsecured retail slippages to remain elevated for 1-2 quarters before stabilizing
items.quote: So unsecured will remain at that level for the next 1 or 2 quarters.

items.statement: 40-45% of retail gross slippages from unsecured portfolio
items.quote: Out of the total around INR 800 crores Gross slippage we had in this quarter, around 40% -45% is actually coming from the unsecured.

items.statement: Added 9 new branches in Q1 FY25, nearly 140 since January 2023
items.quote: We remain committed to judiciously expand our distribution and added nearly 140 new branches since January '23 in CASA rich clusters including 9 in Quarter 1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Retail plus SME to Wholesale advances ratio maintained at 60:40
items.quote: Within Advances, the ratio of Retail plus SME segment Advances against Wholesale segment Advances, (Mid and Large corporates) remained at level of 60:40, in line with our guidance.

items.statement: New retail disbursements accreting 80-100 bps higher spread than portfolio
items.quote: You would see that the spread is already close to 80 to 100 basis points. So the new disbursements are already accreting almost 80 to 100 basis points more than what the portfolio is at.

items.statement: Warrant exercise by Carlyle and Advent affiliates boosted CET1 by ~100 bps
items.quote: I am pleased to also report the exercise of outstanding warrants by CA Basque and Verventa Holdings, which are the funds affiliated and managed by Carlyle and Advent International, which boosted the Bank's CET1 by ~100 basis points.

items.statement: Corporate advances grew 13.8% YoY and 6.3% QoQ as legacy rundown slowed
items.quote: Corporate Advances in line with our recent guidance and which was up by 13.8% Y-o-Y and 6.3% quarter-on-quarter decline seen over the last few years.

items.statement: Expects net addition of 50 screens in FY25 with 120 gross additions and 70 exits
items.quote: For FY '25, the company expects to open 120 new screens and exit 70 screens resulting in a net addition of 50 new screens.

items.statement: Implementing capital-light growth model by partnering with developers for joint capex investment
items.quote: As guided last quarter, we are been selective in new screen additions and gradually implementing a capital-light growth model by partnering with developers and jointly investing in new screen capex.

items.statement: Q2 started strong with Kalki spillover and strong lineup across languages; no major event disruptions expected
items.quote: With Kalki's spill over and the visibility of a great lineup ahead across the languages, Q2 has started off on a great note. We see no other major event disruptions that could hamper the release calendar.

items.statement: Ticket prices increased ~4% in Q1 but ATP declined 5% due to lack of blockbusters; strong uptick post Kalki
items.quote: We did pass on the inflation-led increase in ticket prices to the customers. So in fact, the ticket prices were increased by about 4%.

items.statement: Fixed costs up 7% YoY; same-store fixed cost growth 2.5%; rental escalation 3.7% on same cinemas
items.quote: So on our fixed cost, actually, if you look at our total fixed cost, it has gone up by 7% compared to last year quarter 1. And if we further break that down into like-for-like same-store basis, the same-store growth is only about 2.5%.

items.statement: 15% of current screens are premium formats; 15-20% of new screen additions will be premium formats
items.quote: New screen additions that we are doing, we are adding anywhere between 15% to 20% of new screens in premium or special f ormat screens

items.statement: Karnataka 1-2% cess media report not confirmed as government order; industry engaging with authorities
items.quote: We've been in touch with the government officers. We reached out to the relevant mini stry. And so far, there is no confirmation that this is a definitive government order

items.statement: Monetizing two non-core office assets for INR 300-350 crore; bids received, negotiations ongoing
items.quote: So about 300 to 350 is what we believe it shall be the capital values of the two assets.

items.statement: Re-releases contributed ~12 lakh admissions in Q1; expanding curated film festivals across all geographies
items.quote: This quarter, we contributed close to about 12 lakh admissions coming in from the re-releases itself. So we believe that this is a funnel, which should be truly irrigated, and we will be working on this very vigorously now going forward.

items.statement: Expects similar full-year admissions as FY24 if remaining films perform per original estimates
items.quote: I think Q1 got impacted because the films which were earlier scheduled to be released in Q1 got shifted. So as far as the full year picture goes, what we had earlier estimated, we feel that if the films which are sch eduled to be released in the remaining part of the year, if they perform as per our original estimates, then we should be doing similar admissions as we did in last financial

items.statement: Theatrical window harmonization across regions has consensus but no timeline; South at 4 weeks vs 8 weeks elsewhere
items.quote: We've had some positive conversations with respect to increasing windows, making them consistent across the country. We would not put any timelines to it.

items.statement: New screens typically reach cinema-level EBITDA breakeven within 6-9 months; majority of year-old screens profitable
items.quote: Typically, they start becoming profitable at EBITDA level -- at cinema EBITDA level within 6 to 9 months of opening. And payback periods, et cetera, will vary depending on where the screen is and what sort of formats they are operating.

items.statement: Content pipeline for Q2-Q4 looks strong with many Q1 films pushed forward; full recovery to pre-COVID levels expected next financial year
items.quote: Fortunately, Q2, Q3 and Q4 is looking fairly strong also partly because a lot of films, which were coming in Q1 were pushed to Q2 or Q3. Therefore, it's looking fairly crowded, but we believe the next calendar year and the next financial year will -- is when the content pipeline will be fully back to where it used to be pre-COVID.

items.statement: Bulk of cost synergies from merger reflected in P&L; revenue synergies dependent on footfall recovery
items.quote: I think bulk of it from a cost perspective is reflected in the P&L. I think the revenue-related synergies would also be a function of the recovery on footfalls.

items.statement: Ad revenue grew ~5% YoY driven by Kalki and off-screen sponsorships; expect growth in Q2-Q3 with bigger releases
items.quote: Overall, as well, we looked at not only on-screen, but offscreen sponsorship deals with certain clients where we were playing classics and rereleases. So because of all of that effort, the team was able to deliver this 5% growth.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue guidance of INR1,400-1,500 crores, EBITDA of INR230-260 crores, and exit Q4 EBITDA of INR80-90 crores (20-22% margin).
items.value: Revenue INR1,400-1,500 cr; EBITDA INR230-260 cr; Exit Q4 EBITDA INR80-90 cr
items.quote: We continue to reaffirm our guidance for our outlook for our full year. We expect revenues to be in the range of INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores, with our EBITDA in the range of INR230 crores to INR260 crores and with an exit Q4 EBITDA expected to be in the INR80 crores to INR90 crores level, approximately 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped due to inventory reduction but expected to return to 48% in H2 FY25.
items.quote: So, we said you should estimate that our gross margins will get back to 48% in H2.

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR160 crores in Q1 (INR40 crores from free cash); target year-end net debt under INR500 crores and debt/EBITDA under 2x.
items.value: Debt reduction INR160 cr; Target net debt <INR500 cr; Debt/EBITDA <2x
items.quote: We have reduced debt by about INR160 crores, almost INR40 crores of that coming from free cash generation through the quarter. With a targeted further cash debt reduction from cash flows, we expect end of the year debt adjusted for the uncalled money of the rights to be under INR500 crores and significantly better than our Debt to EBITDA guidance of under 3 times, we should be now comfortably guid

items.statement: Vizag facility retrofit capex amount not finalized; will be funded internally without additional borrowing; update expected next quarter.
items.quote: We don't have the exact numbers as the work is being conducted by consultants. So, we will probably be able to update that in the next quarter. But we would not need to borrow any additional monies to achieve this.

items.statement: Regulated markets revenue share back to 75%+; CRAMS currently 5-8% of revenue, targeting ~10% next year.
items.quote: Well, at this time, we are still in the 5% to 8% range. But based on our confidence and RFP that we expect this to be to grow to about 10% in the next year.

items.statement: Ibuprofen pricing has come down but inventory normalized; Pondicherry facility fully utilized at ~5,000 tons; Vizag retains 3,000-ton ibuprofen block.
items.quote: To answer your specific point on pricing, the pricing has come down, but we do not operate in that market where there is intense competition. And the urge for us to do that earlier and which also caused a lot of trouble for us has been removed by the fact that we have shut the tap from the Vizag facility.

items.statement: Biosecure Act relevant only to biologics, not small molecules; sustained low crude prices expected to improve margins.
items.quote: As the law correctly calls itself The Biosecurity Act, this is only relevant to biologics, and it is not so relevant to

items.statement: Q1 adjusted EBITDA INR50 crores (14% margin) vs reported INR42 crores; difference due to non-recurring Vizag/R&D costs.
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA reported is INR50 crores against a reported EBITDA of INR42 crores. And the reason for this is mainly because part of our network optimization, you would have probably seen in our deck that was released today, we have mothballed our vizag facility.

items.statement: Significant number of CRAMS RFPs issued; expecting conversion of some major programs during the year.
items.quote: We are seeing now with a renewed focus on our CRAMS operations, a significant number of RFPs that we have issued. And we hope that during the year, we would have achieved success with some of these major programs.

items.statement: Reaffirmed Project Leap target of ₹20,000 crore revenue by FY26; new mid-term guidance to be released during FY25
items.quote: We had this target of reaching ₹20,000 crores of top-line by FY26. We exited the previous year at a top-line of about ₹18,000 crores. And that is where we believe that we should be either able to achieve or beat the guidance ahead of its time.

items.statement: International business target of 10% contribution to consolidated revenue by FY26 maintained
items.quote: As part of the Project Leap, we target to reach 10% of contribution from international business for FY26.

items.statement: Capex guidance of ₹1,000-1,100 crore for FY25 maintained; Q1 spend ₹280 crore; expect to be at higher end of range
items.quote: No, there is no change. As you would have seen, during the first quarter, we've done capex of about ₹280 crores. So, we are on track to do the capex on our guided range of ₹1,000 crores to ₹1,100 crores for the year.

items.statement: Wires & Cables long-term EBITDA margin guidance 11-13%; near-term expectation 12-14% due to operating leverage
items.quote: See, our guided range on cables & wires for the long term is 11% to 13%. But we also think that because as of now, we are realizing better operating leverage, we should be able to generate somewhere between 12% to 14% at EBITDA level.

items.statement: EPC business sustainable operating margin expected in high single digits over medium to long term
items.quote: The annual sustainable operating margin for this business is expected to remain in the high single digits over the medium to long term.

items.statement: FMEG advertising and promotion spends guided at 3-5% of B2C top-line annually
items.quote: At an annual level, our advertising and promotion spends will continue to be within our guided range of 3% to 5% of the B2C top-line.

items.statement: Domestic Wires & Cables volume growth ~10% YoY in Q1 FY25 on high base; expect improvement in coming quarters as commodity prices stabilize
items.quote: The domestic Wires & Cables business registered a volume growth of about 10% while the value growth, because of the increased commodity prices, was there but to a large extent, it was negated because of the effect it had on sales.

items.statement: Strong real estate upcycle expected to drive wires demand growth over next 4-8 quarters
items.quote: We do believe that there should be a pickup in the demand for wires over the course of the next few quarters. And if that pans out, there should be an improvement in the mix more towards wires going ahead.

items.statement: EPC contribution expected to normalize to mid-to-high single digits of consolidated revenue from current 10% in Q1
items.quote: Going ahead, on a consistent basis, if you take a yearly view, the contribution from the EPC business will range in mid to high single digit.

items.statement: FMEG mix: fans & lights 50-55%, switches & switchgears high-teens, conduit pipes & fittings similar, others single digits
items.quote: As far as the mix is concerned, the fans and lights both of them are the larger contributors within the FMEG segment contributing somewhere between 50% and 55% of the FMEG top-line.

items.statement: International business softness in largest geography (US) due to distribution model transition; recovery expected over few more quarters
items.quote: We've guided that it will take some more quarters for the new model to stabilize. So once, hopefully, that is done, the sales from that geography should recover back to its normal levels.

items.statement: Freight cost increases compressing international margins; expected to be temporary and normalize
items.quote: What has also happened is the freight costs have increased over the past few quarters. And hence, when you compare this, the margin profile of international business in Q1 of this year versus Q1 of last year, we had that additional impact.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to normalize to 50-55 days from current 64 days as inventory moderates
items.quote: We believe 50 days to 55 days of working capital days is what is an optimum working capital cycle for us. Within that, the inventory days will be somewhere closer to about 100 days.

items.statement: Board reconstituted Audit and NRC committees to comprise only Independent Directors for enhanced governance
items.quote: Both these committees will now fully comprise of Independent Directors, in-line with globally accepted best governance practices.

items.statement: India Ratings upgraded credit rating outlook to 'positive' from 'on watch with negative implication'
items.quote: India Ratings has improved the outlook on our credit rating to 'positive' from the earlier 'on watch with negative implication'.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to be 13%-13.5% for current year
items.quote: as Mr. Chari said this is what at least for the current year, this is what we are seeing, 13%-13.5% will play between these two numbers.

items.statement: Cash outflow of close to Rs. 100 crore for Dahej expansion projects this year
items.quote: Overall, we will have an outflow of close to about Rs. 100 crore.

items.statement: Dahej expansion including 20,000 tons HPPC capacity and 30,000 MT ethoxylation capacity expected to be completed by end of current year
items.quote: Moving forward, our expansion projects at Dahej are progressing as planned and are expected to be completed by the end of the current year.

items.statement: FY26-27 expected to be the right year for 100% utilization of new capacities
items.quote: But I think as we have said in earlier calls also, FY26-27 should be the right year for us to see 100% utilization of those capacities.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning chemical business targeting Rs. 250 crore this year, Q1 was Rs. 60 crore
items.quote: Institutional cleaning chemical this year, we are expecting it to be Rs. 250 crore, the 1st Quarter was about Rs. 60 crore.

items.statement: EBITDA margin dropped to 13.3% from 14.1% due to higher freight, travel, maintenance and selling costs
items.quote: Our EBITDA has improved by 12.5% to Rs. 64.9 crore from Rs. 57.7 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 13.3% compared to 14.1% in the previous year.

items.statement: Prices are stable with slight price cuts in some areas to drive volumes
items.quote: Prices are more or less stable now. There are some places where we have taken slight price cuts just to get into the volume game, but overall prices seem to be stable now.

items.statement: Healthy demand seen in both domestic and export markets for HPPC and Textile segments
items.quote: Both the markets we see healthy demand both domestic and in exports. As I said earlier, the home textile markets especially from the US, the orders are full with our current customers in India and also in Bangladesh.

items.statement: Exports grew ~50% YoY, now 24-25% of revenue, targeting 25-30% range for next 2 years
items.quote: If you see overall the business itself is growing, so it's growing both on the domestic as well as on the exports. But if you see, I think, last year Q1 our exports would have been 20% of our revenue. Today, this quarter it's almost 24%-25%.

items.statement: No provision for Rs. 25 crore GST penalty notice, appealing order, confident of favorable outcome
items.quote: No, there will not be any provision. That's an order which has been passed, as per the department it's an IGST refund, which they claim to be erroneous. We have taken proper legal views on the order which has come, and we are now going to appeal against this order with the higher authority of commissioner appeal, and we are quite hopeful of getting a favorable order on this.

items.statement: Freight costs up 35-40% YoY, container shortages and shipping delays persist as new normal
items.quote: if you see YoY it would have definitely increased about 35%-40% of what it was in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Ethoxylation utilization at 90%+ at both Tristar and Unitop sites, overall average utilization 55-60%
items.quote: On ethoxylation side, our utilizations are at 90% plus at both the sites of Tristar and Unitop.

items.statement: New Dubai subsidiary incorporated for global expansion, may start with marketing then manufacturing
items.quote: We incorporated the subsidiary in Dubai primarily for any global expansion that we may plan going forward. So, rather than holding it through India, we currently incorporated this subsidiary.

items.statement: Working capital at 90-100 days is new normal, hoping for some release by September
items.quote: And as we said in the last 2 earnings call, between 90-100 days is a new normal which we should consider.

items.statement: HPPC and TSC segments both grew 21% YoY, AHN flat due to industry headwinds
items.quote: We are especially pleased with the outstanding performance of our HPPC segment, which achieved a robust 21% growth. items.statement: DCCDL capex of Rs 1,800 crore for FY25; expected to grow 18-20% annually over next 2-3 years
items.quote: On DCCDL this year's CAPEX will be 1,800 crores and going forward in the next 2-3 years this will go up by about 18%-20% from this ballpark figure of 2,000 crores.

items.statement: Residual capex of Rs 700 crore each for three DLF malls and Atrium Place JV with Hines
items.quote: So, the residual CAPEX on the three malls that DLF is constructing is about 700 crores. And the residual CAPEX on the Atrium Place which is a JV with Hines is again about 700 odd crores.

items.statement: Embedded margins for new launches in late 30s%; LUX 5 expected to bring margins back to mid-40s%
items.quote: Our embedded margins for new product launch continue in the late 30s and hopefully with the LUX 5 during the later part of this year we should be back to the mid-40s that we have charted ourselves for.

items.statement: No slowdown seen in luxury segment; bookings backed by Rs 50 lakh booking amount and 35-40% collections within 9 months; negligible re-trade
items.quote: So, I feel based on all of that our price points stay where they are. Also Mr. Tyagi had made a mention yesterday also that if you have seen our collections have been on an all-time high, it has been a record collections this quarter as well.

items.statement: No price exhaustion; global demand base with 25% NRI contribution; secondary market transactions at Rs 30,000-50,000 per sq ft validate pricing
items.quote: No exhaustion. If you are saying again, I don't work in one geography Pritesh. So, for me as I said to you again, I repeat the whole world is one playing field for me.

items.statement: Receivables of Rs 21,000 crore to be collected from launched projects; cost to complete Rs 10,500-11,000 crore with Rs 5,000 crore already in RERA accounts
items.quote: Ballpark our receivables of the projects that we have launched till the 30 th June is about 21,000 crores have to be collected. We have about 10,500-11,000 crores is our total cost to complete.

items.statement: Construction outflow on DevCo side expected north of Rs 800 crore per quarter from Q3 FY25
items.quote: I think our construction is on an ongoing basis. Yes, we believe that on a full total basis from Q3, the construction outflow on the DevCo side should be a number north of 800 crores.

items.statement: Quarterly collections expected to stay in Rs 2,900-3,000 crore range for next two quarters
items.quote: Again, the new launches could occasionally provide a bubble but ballpark this 2,900 to 3,000 crores is I think what a quarterly collection for the next two quarters at least should stay at.

items.statement: Atrium Place rentals of Rs 240-250 crore in FY26; steady state Rs 580-600 crore; three DLF malls to add Rs 300 crore when fully operational
items.quote: The rentals next year will be in the ballpark of 240-250 crores though when all the four blocks are completed on a steady state, the rental will be about 580 to 600 crores.

items.statement: Ireo land parcels: 20-acre license transfer nearing completion; 7-acre plotted-to-group-housing conversion underway; launch targeted early next calendar year
items.quote: So, I think by the time both of them are done, we expect it to be end of this calendar definitely for sure if not end of this fiscal and hence the plan to launch it in the early part of next year.

items.statement: Free operating cash flow exceeded Rs 2,500 crore in Q1 FY25 across DevCo and Cyber City
items.quote: really if you see between our DLF and Cyber City numbers together, we did in excess of 2,500 crores of free operating cash flow during the quarter.

items.statement: LUX 5 pricing expectations rationalized upward; Privana family, Mumbai and Goa pricing unchanged from last quarter
items.quote: What's happened is that, I think clearly we were understating the pricing expectations from LUX 5 and we have rationalized them now.

items.statement: SEZ portfolio leasing momentum to pick up in next 3-4 quarters; office vacancy target of 6-7% by year-end from current 8%
items.quote: I am cautiously optimistic that in the next three-four quarters this will show a lot of traction. I will also share that we have sort of the rental rates for the non SEZ or the non-processing declared areas are slightly better than the rates that we get on SEZ.

items.statement: We should grow around 13% to 15% in revenues and hover around 9% to 10% EBITDA margins for the year.
items.value: 13% to 15% revenue growth; 9% to 10% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We do not give a guidance as such, but we always said that we should grow around 13% to 15% in revenues. And margins, we have largely come back. I think we should hover around between 9% to 10% EBITDA margins for the year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 36.3% in Q1 FY25, up 380 bps YoY, driven by pricing actions, softening input prices, and better product mix; recovery is largely complete.
items.quote: We reported a gross margin of 36.3% in this quarter, an improvement of 380 basis points Y-o-Y. This is due to a combination of pricing action, softening input prices and better product mix. The recovery in margin is now largely complete.

items.statement: Price hikes of ~2% taken in Q4 FY24 and ~2% in Q1 FY25 to offset commodity cost increases; further hikes ongoing and may be landed this month.
items.quote: We had improved our margins through the realization of input cost benefits towards the last quarter of last year and we had taken some price increase, I think, it was about 2-odd percent in quarter four of last year. items.statement: Stabilizer long-term CAGR expected at 8-9%; digital UPS and solar rooftop growing well; wires growth impacted by copper price destocking; kitchen appliances under industry-wide stress for 6-7 quarters.
items.quote: See, for stabilizers, we are expecting, if you look at a very, very long term, that is about 10 years CAGR, It is somewhere around 8% to 9%. And that should be the growth that we also will be working with. But there are years when it goes up substantially higher because of the kind of weather we have.

items.statement: Non-South markets crossed 50% of total revenue in Q1 FY25, growing 30% YoY vs South at 17% YoY; summer-driven product mix boosted Q1 gross margin.
items.quote: In terms of geographies, all regions have done well. The non-South markets delivered a top line growth of 30% Y -o-Y, with revenues in South market growing 17% Y -o-Y. The contribution from non -South markets have crossed 50% in total revenues for this

items.quote: Of late, we are also seeing some firming up of commodity prices and will be taking pricing actions wherever necessary to preserve margins.

items.statement: Outsourcing share of revenue to decline from ~33% to 25% over next 2-3 years as in-house manufacturing scales; zero outsourcing not planned due to seasonal categories.

Naushad Chaudhary: And eventually, in the long term do you plan to make it zero? Mithun K Chittilappilly: No, I think we are always going to have categories where it is not going to make sense for us to manufacture. For example, we will always incubate categories by working with the best par

items.quote: Digital UPS has two components, the inverters and batteries. What I would say, t he battery margins, of course, continued to be under pressure. We have already taken action there in terms of setting up our own facility. I t

items.statement: Wires destocking due to copper price decline in June; restocking requires sustained 2-3% copper price increases over weeks; normalized sales ongoing.
items.quote: See, I think we do not like to talk about an ongoing quarter, but I will just say that today also, I think copper has corrected by about 2% to 3% or something like that. So, the typical behaviour is the trade will try to see if we have reached a bottom. So unless we have sustained 2% to 3% increases in copper prices happening over a few weeks, restocking does not start. Normalized sale is going on

items.statement: Annual sales volume target of 2,10,000 tons for FY25
items.quote: As I said, sales volume has crossed 50,000 tons this quarter and we are in the vicinity of achieving our annual… not in the vicinity, it is likelihood that we will achieve our annual target of 2,10,000 tons of steel.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs.7,000-10,000 for FY25 and Rs.8,000-11,000 from next year post capex
items.quote: This year, Rs. 7000 to Rs. 10,000, next year maybe Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 11,000.

items.statement: Capacity expansion with Kocks block and new reheating furnace on track; two major shutdowns planned in July and Q3/Q4
items.quote: So, those are like capacity expansion by putting up Kocks block and new Re-heating furnace is going on as per plan and things at this moment look quite under control.

items.statement: 55 MW solar power plant purchase agreement signed, expected commissioning by March 2025
items.quote: we have already signed our purchase agreement for setting up 55 MW power plant. Hopefully, it will be in place by March '25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA Rs.48 crores, up 31.71% YoY; realization Rs.82,000 per ton
items.quote: EBITDA is a good number; it is Rs. 48 crores, and it has increased by 31.71%

items.statement: Raw material prices up 8-10% in Q1, neutralized by inventory gains; prices fell in July, inventory valuation loss possible in Q2
items.quote: Raw material prices in Q1, raw material prices was up by 8% to 10%. Its impact on profitability was neutralized by the compensate increase in inventory valuations.

items.statement: Gas cost reduced 40-45% after switching from THINK Gas to GAIL; power tariff up 3% from June 15, increasing annually
items.quote: It is currently lower by about 40%, 45% in terms of pricing.

items.statement: Maruti indicated EV penetration scaled down from 25-30% to 15%, supporting IC engine demand outlook
items.quote: We had a conference our team attended with Maruti, which they have shared that maybe in the things to come the EV penetration, which was envisaged at 30% or 25%, will be about 15%.

items.statement: Billet capacity tested at 2,60,000 MT/annum; 90% yield to rolled product; 25% of rolled goes to bright bars
items.quote: in Q4 FY24 and in Q1 FY25 we tested our capability to achieve the target of 2,60,000 MT per annum, that has been tested and we have been able to achieve these targets.

items.statement: OEM price negotiations ongoing; OEMs benchmarking lower raw material costs; price decrease discussions not finalized
items.quote: Price decrease from OEMs in this quarter, still, discussions are going on by our marketing team with the OEM teams and still there is no final decision on this.

items.statement: Scrap supply gap of 8-10 million tons/annum met by imports; new large steel plant in Ludhiana may increase scrap competition
items.quote: normally the gap between the scrap requirement and domestic supply is around 8-10 million tons per annum and this much amount of scrap is always imported.

items.statement: Greenfield plant still under discussion, no final decision taken
items.quote: Greenfield plant is still under discussion. No final decision has been taken.

items.statement: Exports around 10% of total sales including indirect exports to Aichi Forging; Thailand market subdued, exploring Europe for green steel demand
items.quote: our exports are in the vicinity of around 10% of the total sales including the indirect export of Aichi.

items.statement: Circular economy initiative with major OEM to source scrap directly for steel production
items.quote: He's spearheading another initiative, which is the circular economy with the major OEMs. Circular economy means that we will be getting the scrap from them which will be coming to us and we will be using that scrap to make the steel for them and steel so made will go back to them.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio at 0.12, expected to remain in same range with expansions due to working capital reduction
items.quote: our debt-equity ratios are well within the range; it is close to 0.12. And going forward also with the expansions we are expecting to be in the same range because of savings or a reduction in the working capital.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 18-20% and EBITDA margin range of 15-16% maintained for FY25
items.quote: We will be -- as of now, the same guidance which we have given, that 18%, 20% i n the revenue guidance. And EBITDA last quarter was 16.6%, which was higher than our average margin. items.statement: Particleboard plant expected to start commercial production in Q3 FY25
items.quote: On the particleboard plant, as mentioned, we should be able to start the plant in Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Peak debt estimated at INR925-950 crores in FY25 as particleboard project completes
items.quote: As per our estimate, peak debt will be in this year only because the project particleboard project will get over in this year. So we believe that our peak debt will be in the range of around INR925 crores to INR950 crores, in that range.

items.statement: Particleboard project targets 15-18% ROCE at full utilization by year 3-4 with 20-24% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We believe that in terms of when we reach the full utilization level, which will happen in t he third or fourth year kind of a thing, then we can have that margin in the range of around 15% to 18% ROCE
