items.quote: EBITDA margin for the laminate business stood at 13.6% in this quarter, a degrowth of 120 basis points on a year-on-year basis and a degrowth of 300 basis points on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Plywood prices increased ~4% effective July; laminate price increase under review
items.quote: On the plywood business, we passed on certain costs to the market effective July. So about close to 4% price increases we've done. On the laminate side, we are still reviewing the cost impact and whether we can offset it with higher volume and better value mix.

items.statement: Domestic laminate demand expected to normalize in Q2 FY25 after election and heat disruptions in Q1
items.quote: So our sense is that even this month is looking pr etty decent. So our sense is it should be kind of normalized quarter in Q2, at least on the domestic demand side

items.statement: Export shipments of ~1.5 lakh sheets held back in June due to container unavailability; situation slightly better in July
items.quote: in Q1 -- still at the towards the end of June, we could not be able to ship some of the material, nearly 1.5 lakh sheets, we would not be able to ship. And that situation in July, it's only, I will not say majorly improved, but yes, a little bit better than Jun e end

items.statement: Laminate realization improved to INR1,105/sheet in Q1; focus on premiumization and value mix to offset cost pressures
items.quote: Our average realization for the quarter was at INR1,105 per sheet.

items.statement: Container availability and freight cost volatility persist due to geopolitical issues; no clear timeline for normalization
items.quote: It's difficult to, as of now, say when the situation will become normal because it's not in our hand, it's more of a geopolitical situation, which is creating this trouble.

items.statement: Timber costs at highest levels, impacting plywood and particleboard margins; expected to settle by particleboard commissioning
items.quote: As the things stand as of now, the raw material cost, the timber cost is at the highest level till now, and that's a cycle. And we believe that it will settle down by the time we come into the arc, commercial products in the starts.

items.statement: Revenue potential of INR4,000-4,200 crores at full capacity utilization by FY28 including particleboard
items.quote: We believe that at the current prices, we will be in the range of around INR4,000 crores to INR4,200 crores. And we believe that if everything goes as per our plan, that should happen by, let's say, in around FY '28.

items.statement: Plywood capacity utilization expected to reach ~40% for full year FY25
items.quote: For the year as a whole, we expect that our utilization will be in the range of around 40%.

items.statement: Laminate capacity utilization at 83% in Q1; brownfield expansion possible at Gujarat and Naidupeta plants
items.quote: We are running at around 83% capacity utilization as a whole, and we have gone up in the past 108%, 110%. So we have around 17%, 18% -- sorry, around 25% capacity in our hand.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 65 days in Q1 FY25 from 72 days in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Our net working capital days stood at 65 days in this quarter as compared to 72 days in quarter 1 last year.

items.statement: VNB margin stood at 24.0% in Q1-FY2025, up 7.8% YoY to ₹4.72bn VNB
items.quote: The VNB for Q1-FY2025 grew by 7.8% year-on-year to ₹ 4.72 billion. The VNB margin stood at 24.0%.

items.statement: ULIP share of APE rose to 51.4% from 38.8% YoY; non-linked savings fell to 16.8% from 27.7%
items.quote: Contribution from linked savings product to overall APE increased from 38.8% in Q1-FY2024 to 51.4% in Q1-FY2025 on account of customer preference shifting towards unit products from non-linked products.

items.statement: Annuity share of APE increased to 10.9% from 6.2% YoY, driven by regular premium annuity with 100% money-back feature
items.quote: Our annuity business contribution increased from 6.2% in Q1-FY2024 to 10.9% in Q1-FY2025. Within annuity, we continue to witness a tilt towards regular premium annuity over single premium annuity.

items.statement: Retail protection APE grew 1.8% YoY in Q1 but 28.3% CAGR over two years; expect strong growth trajectory going forward
items.quote: The overall protection APE stood at ₹ 3.55 billion and contributed 18.1% to overall APE in Q1-FY2025. Retail protection business grew by 1.8% in Q1-FY2025, with the number of policies growing by 6.7%. On a two-year basis, retail protection APE has grown at a CAGR of 28.3% for us. Retail protection continues to be one of our focus areas, and we expect a strong growth trajectory going forward.

items.statement: No specific full-year growth guidance given; aim to deliver alpha over market sustainably
items.quote: No. Our idea is to be able to work sustainably and to look at delivering an alpha over the market.

items.statement: Surrender value regulation effective Oct 1, 2024; impact muted as non-linked is only 17% of portfolio; trail/level commission products launched to align stakeholders
items.quote: There will not be any impact on margins because of surrender guideline changes from 1st October, Sanketh, if you can look at product mix slide, you will note that that side of business is only 17% of our portfolio.

items.statement: Expense allocation methodology change (₹446 cr) has no material VNB impact and no par impact; statutory liabilities affected
items.quote: This 7 doesn't really have any material impact on the VNB at this point. The larger impact, as we had disclosed, is on the statutory liabilities

items.statement: Protection pricing actions taken continuously in specific cohorts; media reports of price hikes reflect industry nature
items.quote: We keep looking at where we are in the market space. We keep looking at various segments. We look at how the emerging trends are in each of them from the risk and a profitability perspective and we keep taking price actions in specific cohorts.

items.statement: Credit life growing ~2x banking credit growth at 27-28% YoY; driven by new partner additions and differentiated propositions
items.quote: I think that this business has been almost growing twice the rate of credit growth in the banking setup. So, there we are quite happy with the progress of the 27% and 28% growth that we have on the credit life business and that is largely on account of new partner additions that we are doing consistently.

items.statement: Non-linked split roughly two-thirds par, one-third non-par; non-par volumes stressed due to market buoyancy favoring ULIPs
items.quote: So, roughly about two-third, one-third is where the par, non-par split is actually, and the decline that you see in the non-linked product line is because of the stress that you have seen in terms of volumes of the non-par product.

items.statement: VNB margin trajectory uncertain until new products finalized and distributor conversations conclude; focus on win-win-win for all stakeholders
items.quote: It is still a little too early to call, primarily because of two fronts. One, the products are still in a development phase at this stage and conversations with our distributors is still live at this stage. So, until these come to an end, it is a little difficult to identify where the margin would be.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 20% to 25% for FY25
items.quote: At the end of Q1 FY '25, our AUM stood at INR178.41 billion, up by 22%, which aligns with the target to grow our AUM by 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Endeavour to maintain 5% spread going forward
items.quote: Our endeavour is to maintain the 5% spread going forward.

items.quote: Our margin, NIM as a percentage of total asset during Q1 FY '25 stood at 7.31%.

items.quote: Our incremental borrowing cost increased by 30 bps Y-o-Y and 17 bps Q-o-Q to 8.31%, indicating the cost of borrowing peaking out in line with the benchmark rates.

items.quote: And yield if you see, last quarter to this quarter we have almost a 17-18 bps higher yield on the new business we got in this quarter.

items.quote: The robust 25% Y-o-Y growth in the sanction serves as a clear indicator of our robust trajectory.

items.quote: And in the coming quarters, we'll have the sanction to disbursement ratio really covering up to the normal levels of 85%-87%.

items.quote: we continue to be at aroun d 5% to 5.5%. And I think that is backed up by on an annual basis

items.statement: GNPA at 1.01% and 1+DPD at 3.65% in Q1 FY25, credit cost at 20 bps
items.quote: Our asset quality continues to be pristine with 1+DPD at 3.65% as of June 24, down by 3 bps over Q1 FY '24, our GNPA stood at 1.01% in Q1 FY '25 and credit cost remained at 20 bps.

items.statement: Total tech transformation capex of INR45-50 crore over two years, final year of capitalization in FY25
items.quote: All put together is a total capex in the company roughly in two years something we already capitalized, something will be capitalized put together everything will be INR45 crore around capitalization INR45 crore to INR50 crore capitalization.

items.quote: The focus on the ticket size which is going to be less than INR15 lakhs to contribute higher and even in the buckets which we are their incremental increase granularly on the yields or the disbursement yield is our endeavour.

items.quote: To meet long-term business growth, we have progressed on the co-lending tie-up with a PSU bank.

items.statement: Branch count to increase by 10% over three years, manpower increase less than 10% for productivity leverage
items.quote: Branch count will increase by 10% in let's say, we are targeting three years. As well as the manpower will increase by less than 10%.

items.statement: Target pre-IndAS EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY25 at consolidated level
items.quote: we endeavor to be EBITDA breakeven, pre-IndAS. Spencer's

items.quote: just without contextualizing this, without these 49 stores, our store EBITDA would double from the current level.

items.quote: in terms of absolute numbers, we are looking at adding 8 to 10 stores in a 12 month period on a year-on-year basis focused on East and Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Maintain mid-single digit SSSG guidance for Spencer's in East and UP from Q3 onward
items.quote: we Spencer’s would continue our guidance of mid-single digit SSSG in the geographies of East and UP, where we will continue to operate from Quarter 3 onward

items.statement: 19.5% gross margin sustainable for Spencer's format
items.quote: We strongly believe 19 .5% is a sustainable level of margin given the fact that we are not position ed as a value discounter

items.statement: Target adding 100,000 sq ft trading area per year to reach 1 million sq ft in 24 months
items.quote: we are very confident that over the next 12 to 18 months, we will be able to add at the rate of 100,000 square feet per year to bring back our total trading area to close t o 1 million square feet in 24 months

items.statement: Pipeline of 6-7 Natures Basket store openings through the year
items.quote: We will continue to have store openings here as we are looking at a total number of 6 to 7 stores coming on board through the year.

items.quote: we have about 49 stores accounting for close to 22% of the business and therefore, it was a very well thought through and considered decision. However, the point to note is that these 49 stores accounted for close to Rs. 56 crores of losses at a regional EBITDA level

items.quote: Today, we are with this round of further optimization, we will get to a level of close to 6.3% which is I would say a respectable number as far as the overhead cost as the contribution to total sales would be.

items.quote: we are almost 35% lower in headcount and cost by the time we complete this exercise in Quarter 3.

items.statement: Natures Basket expects high single digit growth to continue through FY25
items.quote: So, overall, we expect definitely high single digit growth continuing for Natures Basket to deliver.

items.statement: Consolidated debt at Rs 800 cr (Spencer's Rs 700 cr, Natures Basket Rs 100 cr)
items.quote: The current debt position, yes. So, at Spencer's standalone, it is around Rs. 700 crores and at Natures Basket it is at least about Rs. 100 crores, at a consol level, about Rs. 800 crores.

items.statement: Target Rs 100 cr annualized EBITDA improvement from store exits and cost optimization
items.quote: we believe that this significant operating turnaround where we are talking about a swing of roughly Rs. 100 crores EBITDA improvement will provide us op tions for capital raise enabling recapitalization of our balance sheet

items.statement: Target 20% asset book growth for FY25
items.quote: Our focus is towards maintaining the guidance given on our previous communication of 20% asset book growth and the full year ROE at 20%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 at 1.7%
items.quote: In the beginning of the year, we had guided that our credit cost would be in the range of 1.7%.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY25 at 9%
items.quote: I would just like to conclude by saying and reiterating that we are looking for this financial year to grow our outstandings by 20%, to maintain a 20% return on equity, 9% NIM, credit costs within 1.70 percentages.

items.statement: Secured book target of 35% by end of FY25

items.quote: Our future-ready loan origination system was launched in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 NIM at 9.3%

items.quote: COF, cost of funds for Q1 financial year '25 is at 7.5%, marginally elevated from last quarter as Q4 FY '24 had a onetime benefit of reversal of interest expense.

items.quote: We do believe normalcy will be restored by end of H1 FY '25 and higher volume generation will be achievable from Q3 onwards.

Also, the fact that yes, there has been a slowdown in the US market which we now expect to have a recovery towards in the Q2, Q3 and Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Alloy wheel penetration expected to rise from 36-38% to 39-40% in FY25, targeting 45-50% medium term
items.quote: Within this year, we expected that the alloy wheel penetration will move from say at 36%, 37% to maybe 39%, 40% which has not happened in this financial year because of the cost pressures or maybe the OEMs are not able to sell those cars in that numbers and they are trying to have different kind of a connotation towards pleasing customers. But we are fairly confident with the industry moving towar

items.statement: Hydrogen peroxide plant started trial runs, expected to commission shortly; Epichlorohydrin plant trial runs in Q2 FY25

items.statement: Epoxy and other downstream products under active evaluation, awaiting board approval
items.quote: As this round of the CAPEX is nearing completion, we are actively working on starting activities on epoxy and other downstream products including chlorine downstream.

items.statement: Chlor-Alkali PBDIT up to Rs. 133 crore from Rs. 36 crore YoY due to higher volumes and energy cost savings
items.quote: The Chlor-Alkali business revenues were up 18% year -on-year and PBD IT was up at Rs. 133 crore as compared to Rs. 36 crore last year due to higher volumes and significant savings in energy costs led by 44 MW renewable energy and lower coal costs

items.statement: Vinyl PBDIT at Rs. 44 crore vs negative Rs. 3 crore YoY on volume growth and input cost reduction

items.statement: Fenesta PBDIT moderated to Rs. 36 crore from Rs. 40 crore YoY due to higher fixed costs from new capacity and lower B2B volumes
items.quote: PBDIT slightly moderated to Rs. 36 crore as compared to Rs. 40 crore in the last year on account of higher fixed cost s incurred due to setting up of newer revenue platform and enhancing capacities and also due to higher sales promotion and business development expenses

items.statement: Domestic PVC demand robust, grew ~17% in Q1 FY25 driven by agriculture and construction
items.quote: The domestic demand for PVC in India is robust and estimated to have grown by about 17% in this quarter in the wake of agriculture and constructio n activities

items.statement: Caustic demand linked to GDP growth; medium-term outlook positive despite short-term oversupply
items.quote: We are very optimistic that while there is some over capacity in the short term. In the medium term, this capacity will all be absorbed comfortably.

items.statement: ECU currently Rs. 27,000-28,000 range, expected to be range-bound or improve gradually
items.quote: Current ECUs are in the Rs. 27,000-28,000 range and we expect it to be range bound or improve gradually.

items.statement: PVC prices currently Rs. 84,000-85,000; international prices fell from $980 to $910 per MT
items.quote: The current prices are around Rs. 84,000-85,000. So, the international price also has come off. So, let's say in June they were around $980. Currently they are about $910 per metric ton.

items.statement: Fenesta order book up 20% YoY
items.quote: Order book was up by 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: Bioseed PBDIT improved to Rs. 29 crore from Rs. 23 crore on product mix and prices
items.quote: PBDIT has improved to Rs. 29 crore from Rs. 23 crore last year led by the product mix and prices.

items.statement: Sugar exports restricted; stock expected at 8-9 MT vs 5 MT last year; pushing government for export approval
items.quote: For sugar right now, there are extensive talks taking place with the government for allowing exports because as said in the opening remarks, last year our sugar stock on 30 th of September was 5 million tons. And this year is going to between 8 -9 million tons

items.statement: New caustic capacity (850 TPD) to reach 40-50% utilization in H2 FY25; existing capacity at 80-85%
items.quote: In the second half of the year, the expanded capacity we should see a 40% to 50% capacity utilization. And the existing capacity, which is close to about 1800 tons per day, we should be utilizing about 80%-85%.

items.statement: ECH plant commercial production early Q3 FY25; steady ramp by Q3-Q4; material benefit next fiscal year
items.quote: For epichlorohydrin, we should commission the trials in this quarter which is Q2 and commercial production should start in the Q3, maybe early Q3 we should start commercial production.

items.statement: Expect to be above industry growth for full year FY25
items.quote: We continue to expect to be above industry growth for the full year, gaining from the tech-led account focused strategy I talked about.

items.statement: Target sustainable EBIT margin within 14.6% to 16% band
items.quote: We continue to target sustainable EBIT margin within the stated band of 14.6% to 16%, and we will maintain this while investing for growth, with focus on productivity, efficiencies and operating leverage.

items.statement: Q1 EBIT margin at 15%, Silverline acquisition costs impacted margin by 0.8%
items.quote: In this quarter, our EBIT margin stood at 15%. Silverline acquisition costs impacted our margin by 0.8%.

items.statement: TCV wins of $319 million in Q1 FY25 with 3 large deals including one over $100 million
items.quote: We continued with a higher share of proactive deal wins in our TCV wins of $319 million in the first quarter of FY25. The quarter saw 3 large deals, including one large deal of over $100 million in our BFS vertical.

items.statement: Overall pipeline up 22% YoY and 17% QoQ, one-third AI-led
items.quote: Our overall pipeline is up 22% year-over-year and 17% sequentially. All pipeline metrics are green, with broad-based pickup in deals across sectors such as top 10 accounts, non-top 10 accounts, BFS, non-BFS, all geographies as well as across large deals.

items.statement: Launched NeoZeta modernization platform reducing relearning time by over 50% and NeoCrux IDE extension for software engineering productivity
items.quote: We are launching an industry-first modernization platform called Mphasis NeoZetaTM, which is a platform for transforming legacy applications, written in languages like COBOL, Natural or legacy Java, using Gen AI LLMs and LAMs to reduce relearning time by over 50%.

items.statement: BFS grew 1.1% sequentially, Insurance grew 2.4% sequentially, early signs of recovery in mortgage business
items.quote: At an overall company level, BFS was up 1.1% sequentially in Q1, and Docusign Envelope ID: 04 specifically in Direct Ex -DR, BFS was up 0.9% sequentially. Overall, Insurance grew 2.4% sequentially

items.statement: Mortgage recovery timing uncertain, dependent on Fed rate cuts and 30-year mortgage approaching 6% or 5.5%
items.quote: Whether that happens in September or November, I don't really know because I don't have a good handle on what the Fed action will be to drive it.

items.statement: MSCI upgraded ESG rating from BBB to A due to improvements in corporate governance and data security
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that Morgan Stanley Capital International, MSCI, has recognized these efforts and upgraded Mphasis's ESG rating from 'BBB' to 'A'.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 22-24% with EBITDA margin improvement of 100-200 bps
items.quote: On the yearly outlook we continue to guide as I said earlier 22% to 24% revenue growth for FY '25 and 100 bps to 200 bps margin improvement over this current financial year.

items.statement: FY25 capex guided at INR 250 crores with INR 70 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: Q1 capex was close to around INR 70 crores. This is in l ine with our annual plan of INR 250 crores which we announced earlier in the

items.statement: Next 2-3 years capex run rate seen at INR 400-500 crores annually for new plants
items.quote: So you will see something between INR400 crores and INR 500 crores of capex happening in the next couple of years of further accelerated growth.

items.statement: Dialysis machine order book supports target of 400-500 machines in FY25
items.quote: This year we plan to sell close to 400 machines and maybe even go up to 500 depending on how this order book matures, but we have a good traction and we are on track for this kind of growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement guided at 100-200 bps for FY25 driven by higher-margin transformative segments
items.quote: And even the margin we have spoken that there will be an improvement by 100 bps to 150 bps in the current financial year when you look at the year as a whole.

items.statement: Renal business grew 40%+ in Q1, on track for INR 140-150 crores in FY25
items.quote: Renal business in Q1 has increased by over 40%. So this is something very heartening to note. And we are on track to grow from INR90 crores to INR140 crores, INR145 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Export mix shifted to 70% in Q1 from 67% last year, expected to stay around 70/30
items.quote: Last year, exports were around two -third exports, one-third domestic market almost 67% and 33% ratio, b ut in first quarter the ratio has changed. We have 70% exports and almost 30% domestic sales

items.statement: Container shortage and freight rates expected to normalize by Oct-Nov, currently impacting exports
items.quote: And as we hear from industry sources that this container shortage or export freight rates will only come down by October, November. So next two months, three months it's challenging.

items.statement: Board approved QIP up to INR 1,000 crores; majority for capex, 25-30% for inorganic opportunities
items.quote: The Board recently g ave approval to raise up to INR 1,000 crores through QIP process which was done through a board meeting end of June. And most part of the funds will be used for capex

items.statement: US business projected to reach USD 15-20 million in next 3 years with 12-14 FDA approvals
items.quote: We are very hopeful that it will grow as we have projected earlier between USD15 million to USD20 million in the next 3 years' time.

items.statement: Capacity increased from 1.2B to 1.5B units, targeting 1.7-1.8B by year-end
items.quote: The capacity now has increased from 1.2 billion units to 1.5 billion units per year. And by end of the year, we will further increase the capacity to around 1.7 billion to 1.8 billion units for medical devices.

items.statement: Domestic trade sales grew 25% in Q1; domestic growth guided at 20-22% for FY25
items.quote: Domestic growth as I said earlier we are looking at between 20% and 22% overall growth for domestic business in the current financial year, b ut export will be slightly higher

items.statement: China plant revenue under USD 2M, may shut down as lease expires in 18-24 months
items.quote: China plant is a very small plant with less than 40, 50 people and the revenue is under USD2 million from China plant. And the reason we will probably close it down is because of current cost structures in China are much, much higher as compared to India.

items.statement: Price hikes taken only on significant raw material changes; prices generally stable with 20-25% cost advantage vs MNCs in Europe
items.quote: See, It depends on product-to-product very hard to say what is the delta. But I would say, maybe 20%, 25% price differential for sure between Indian companies and large multinational companies.

items.statement: Gamma sterilization plant under construction, expected live by early next year
items.quote: Our gamma sterilization plant is under construction right now and should be live by early next year.

items.quote: We have added 40 plus sales associates in quarter 1 which is in line with our plan to add 100 -plus people in the current financial year and these 40 people have come across mainly in the new verticals of critical care and cardiology.

items.statement: Management expects coking coal price savings of $30-35 per ton in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Further, we are expecting savings in coking coal price in Q2, '25 by around $30 to $35 per ton.

items.statement: Management sees iron ore price reduction of INR500-1,000 per ton in Q2 FY25
items.quote: So the steel price, we have seen the recent auctions, and we are seeing around INR500 to INR1,000 per ton reduction in iron ore price as well.

items.statement: Capex incurred in Q1 FY25 was INR2,796 crores
items.quote: Our capex in the quarter stood at INR2,796 crores.

items.statement: Total project capex incurred to date is INR17,500 crores out of INR31,000 crores
items.quote: So from the capex side, we have already incurred around INR17,500 crores on these projects.

items.statement: No cost escalation expected on 6 MTPA expansion project; contingency built in
items.quote: So we are not expecting any cost escalation on the overall project cost, which we have designed. So whatever we have mentioned we will be completing all projects within that cost.

items.statement: Targeting major facilities (blast furnace, BOF, CRM) completion by Q4 FY25; ancillary facilities in 9-12 months
items.quote: We are targeting to complete the major facility that is blast furnace, BOF, CRM, well, JIND/l r/ STEEL & POWER Jindal Steel & within timeline by Q4 of financial year '25. The remaining ancillary facility will be completed in another 9 to 12

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA for Q1 FY25 was INR2,831 crores, up 13% QoQ
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA for the first quarter, was INR2,831 crores, which is 13% higher on a quarter-on-quarter basis, mainly on account of higher sales volume, higher sales realization and cost efficiency achieved at our plants.

items.statement: Steel NSR increased ~1% QoQ in Q1 FY25; seeing ~1% softening in July
items.quote: Our steel sales realization also saw slight upstick of around 1% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining 2 million tons+ quarterly sales volume; RINL volumes would be incremental
items.quote: No, we are confident on maintaining that volume level.

items.statement: Product mix shifted to 57% long / 43% flat in Q1 FY25 from 68% long / 32% flat a year ago
items.quote: So as compared to the last year of 68% to long and 32% flat. In the first quarter, this financial year, we have been 57% long and 43% flat, if that answers your question.

items.statement: Project delays due to general elections and unprecedented heat wave in Odisha causing workforce demobilization
items.quote: If I was to say this year, be the happening year for the country in terms of general elections. And then also we experienced a very unprecedented heat wave in Odisha. So while they were good times that we could have pulled up our project that we lost because of these 2 larger reasons.

items.statement: Slurry pipeline delayed due to election-related approval delays; targeting completion by end of FY25
items.quote: But again, because of elections, there have been some kind of delays in terms of securing approvals, things are back on track, and we are actually getting on the ground in the right way. And we are hopeful by the end of this financial year, we should see this project also coming up.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR10,462 crores; net debt/EBITDA at 1x; target to maintain 1.5x
items.quote: Our consolidated net debt is INR10,462 crores at the end of quarter 1, which has dropped from INR11,203 crores reported during the last quarter.

items.statement: Utkal C EC increase from 3.37 to 4.78 MTPA in final approval stage; expected in 2-2.5 months
items.quote: we have given a guidance that we would be increasing our EC from 3.37 to potentially 4.78. That would be happening and that's happening on track. We are at the last leg JIND/l r/ STEEL & POWER Jindal Steel & of approvals right now

items.quote: I'm hoping that in the next 2 months' time, we should be in a position to start that.

items.statement: Management targets pre-sales of Rs 8,000-10,000 crores by FY28, implying ~50% CAGR from current levels.
items.quote: My goal is to scale this business, for us to achieve 8,000 to 10,000. That's the raw material.

items.statement: GDV addition target for FY25 is to exceed last year's Rs 4,400 crores, but will be measured and focused on quality deals.
items.quote: My goal is definitely do more than Rs. 4,400 crores that we did last year.

items.statement: Total controllable GDV pipeline is ~Rs 20,000 crores, including signed deals, unsold inventory, land bank, and Thane potential.
items.quote: So 4,000, 4,000, 3,000 and 1,000, so that's 12,000 and Thane we have applied for IITT policy after 63-1A exit, that's 8,000. So, that's 20,000 of GDV that we currently either own or have a path to launching.

items.statement: FY25 launch pipeline includes ~7 projects with Rs 3,000+ crores GDV, led by Vista Phase-II (~Rs 1,500 cr), Navy (~Rs 950-1,000 cr), Citadel Phase-III (~Rs 1,000+ cr), and WestEra (~Rs 500 cr).
items.quote: If you add all of them together it will probably be Rs. (+3,000) crores worth of launches that we will have minimum for the rest of the financial year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 pre-sales jumped 3x to Rs 1,019 crores (71% from new launches), with healthy pipeline; but management cautions against linear extrapolation due to lumpiness.
items.quote: On the sales side we achieved quarterly pre-sales of Rs. 1,019 crores which was last Quarter 1 Financial Year was Rs. 345 crores. It reflects a healthy jump 3x.

items.statement: Residential EBITDA drag from legacy (pre-2020) projects to persist in FY25; meaningful profitability improvement expected from FY26 onward as new IRR-focused projects hit P&L.
items.quote: My feel is from the next financial year, not from the F25 but F26 onward you will start to see the new portfolio projects starting to kick in which will try to absorb the drag a lot more than right now what we are seeing in our P&L and balance sheet.

items.statement: Operating cash flow (pre-land) averages Rs 650 crores/year; land spend FY25 estimated at Rs 700-800 crores (lower if more JDA/redevelopment).
items.quote: If we go into more society redevelopment or JDA kind of projects this will be a slightly lower number other than that it would probably be a healthy Rs. 700 to 800 crores towards land as well.

items.statement: Fundraise discussions underway with Mahindra Group, external fund houses, and global partners; no timeline or structure finalized.
items.quote: There are I would say three four discussion that is going on, given they are internally at Mahindra level, externally with some of the other fund houses as well as some of the global partners who have interest in pursuing India opportunity and India real estate opportunity with a credible responsible player.

items.statement: Approval timelines slowed in Q1 due to elections; execution risk remains on 3-4 year project cycles, but conservative costing and IRR thresholds aim to protect margins.
items.quote: We saw Quarter 1 was I would say slower than what we would have ideally liked in terms of the speed of approval. But we understand many of the officials' business was affected because of elections almost I think six weeks.

items.statement: Net debt (fully consolidated) reduced to Rs 398 crores; net debt/equity 0.21x; cost of debt 8.96% (down from 9.03%).
items.quote: The net debt at consol level as per IndAS would reflect Rs. 570 crores. But when we do a complete consolidation of debt as well as cash the net debt would stand at Rs. 398 crores.

items.statement: Happinest (affordable) inventory liquidation targeted over 2-4 years; strategic focus remains mid-premium and premium segments (~70% of market).
items.quote: I think it will be, we are carefully targeting anywhere from 2 to 4 years. Some of the phases are more recently launched which are part of subsequent phases of promise project.

items.statement: IC&IC leased ~19 acres (Rs 76 crores) in Q1 FY25; Jaipur led with 13 acres (Rs 50 crores).
items.quote: We ended Quarter 1 FY25 with leasing or which is a perpetual leasing sale of roughly 19 acres translated into Rs. 76 crores with MWC Jaipur taking the lead with 13 acres, roughly Rs. 50 crores there and Chennai with around Rs. 27 crores.

items.statement: Revenue recognition for FY25 (ex-IC) estimated at ~Rs 1,400 crores, tied to OC receipts and project completions.
items.quote: I think because linked to OCs etc. it will be around, if I exclude the IC business it will be Rs. (+/–1,400) crores is what we expect for which we are either we have completed waiting for OC or will be completing and will be applying for OC.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 consolidated total income Rs 206.7 crores vs Rs 110.1 crores YoY; PAT Rs 12.7 crores vs loss of Rs 4.3 crores; net operating cash flow Rs 287 crores.
items.quote: We saw that our consolidated total income stood at about Rs. 206.7 crores in Q1 of FY25 and this is a better performance as against the Rs. 110.1 crores that we saw in Q1 FY 24.

items.statement: FY25 CAPEX target is around Rs. 3,500 crores
items.quote: This year, CAPEX target is around Rs. 3,500 crores.

items.statement: Dahej expansion to complete by March 2025 with total CAPEX around Rs. 570 crores
items.quote: by March 25, we expect that expansion to be completed. That means that the to tal CAPEX by that time will be around Rs. 570 crores

items.quote: we may be tying up to the extent of almost Rs. 10,000, Rs. 11,000 crores, or maybe more than that Rs. 12,000 crores.

items.quote: If you look at the long-term commitment at Dahej, it is almost 15.75 MMTPA . 7.5 is our own Rasgas volume and then balance 8.25 million tons is the capacity booking.

items.statement: India gas volume in May-June around 213 MMSCMD vs 188 MMSCMD previous year; moderate LNG prices support demand growth
items.quote: As I was looking at the data in the month of May, June, it is around 213 MMSCMD, which is much, much higher as compared to 188 MMSCMD of volume in the previous year.

items.statement: Q1 inventory gain Rs. 261 crore and trading margin Rs. 58 crore
items.value: 261 crore inventory gain, 58 crore trading margin
items.quote: The inventory gain is Rs. 261 crore this quarter. And the trading margin which we have got is Rs. 58 crore.

items.statement: LNG price increased from $9.50 to around $11.50 driving inventory gain
items.quote: It was $9.50 last time; it is around $11.50 at this point of time. So, there is a difference, $2 difference is there almost.

items.value: Rs. 378 crore (CY2021) and Rs. 798 crore (CY2022) bank guarantees

items.quote: Volumes are going as per the ADP, and we don't see any issue in that.

items.quote: Rs. 129 crore has been booked as provision for the quarter. We are booking this credit loss for each quarter based on our formula.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 15% to 20% for FY25
items.quote: No, I think in terms of demand we still stand by our commitment of 15% to 20% volume growth year-to-year. So FY '24 to FY '25 we feel that we will be able to achieve and do better than what we have predicted it.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining EBITDA margins of approximately 23% plus for forthcoming quarters
items.quote: The EBITDA margin expanded by 70 basis points year-on-year and we are confident of sustaining margins of approximately this 23% plus for the forthcoming quarters.

items.value: INR 500 Crores standalone, INR 135 Crores subsidiaries, INR 100 Crores JV

items.statement: Vande Bharat order of INR 270 Crores to be executed in FY26 and FY27
items.quote: Yes. And it will be in line with whatever Vande Bharat are made. But this -- once this validation of bogie happens it will open also new opportunities for us directly into the Indian Railways.

items.quote: Right now, we are currently operating at around 16% plus EBITDA margin, and there will be a further improvement of 100 basis points to 200 basis points in EBITDA in Multitech Auto going forward.

items.statement: Export realization improved due to product mix change and new customer traction; domestic realization stable currently
items.quote: In terms of exports, I think, in terms of product mix change and addition of new customers, wherein order announcements had been made in previous years have started showing traction and that is the reason realization in exports have improved. In terms of domestic, seeing the current trend, what is available right now, we don't expect any reduction in terms of realization.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis causing INR 20-25 Crores regular impact on shipping costs and inventory
items.quote: No, the impact was -- I think impact was INR 20 Crores and I think still the impact remains similar in the similar range and that has become a regular precedent. So, INR20 Crores to INR 25 Crores will remain always in mid -sea or material -- so, that is

items.statement: Ramkrishna Titagarh JV project cost now INR 1,800 Crores; first production for validation in FY26 last quarter
items.quote: So right now what we are looking at the project cost of the Ramkrishna Titagarh side the project is around INR 1,800 Crores right now. So, the project cost is INR 1,800 Crores.

items.statement: Confident of 15-20% volume growth based on past order wins showing traction and steady customer offtakes
items.quote: Past order wins have already started showing traction in terms of supplies. So, we are very confident that we will be able to meet expectation and do better than what we are estimating in terms of 15% to 20% volume growth.

items.quote: Working capital is around 90 days. Net working capital is around 90 days, and that will continue to remain at 90 days cycle.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 3.5% to 3.7% for the year
items.quote: In any case, our guidance to the market, which we have always said, is that we would be between 3.5% to 3.7% and we stay within the guidance as far as this is concerned.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 at 0.9% to 1%
items.quote: We are still targeting at closer to about overall 1%. This has been our annualized target. But we will be happy if it is a little lesser. But I think we are prepared to digest up to 0.9% to 1%.

items.statement: PCR target of 80% in next 2-3 quarters

items.statement: Aspiration to reach Rs. 1 lakh crore gross advances by March 2026
