items.quote: the labor shortage situation compounded by the fact that there has been a significant wage increase of 3%, I think has presented a complex situation before us.

items.statement: Railway FM contracts loss-making, limited flexibility to exit government tenders
items.quote: There is a bunch of railway contracts, which we are trying to exit. But obviously, being a government tender, there are limitations, and there is only limited flexibility for vendors to step out.

items.statement: VProtect monthly billing ~INR10 crores, ~20% EBITDA margin, 25,000+ installations growing rapidly
items.quote: VProtect business is tracking very well. It has a good pipeline of contracts. It's run rating close to INR10 crores for monthly billing, monthly invoices INR10 crores, close to 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: DAM Capital appointed for Cash Logistics demerger process; documentation ready, clarity expected next quarter
items.quote: DAM Capital has just been appointed to run the process and documentation is more or less ready. Hopefully, in the next quarter, we'll have good clarity around that.

items.statement: Budget provisions for first-time job entrants and PF support seen as positive; awaiting fine print for exact impact
items.quote: the key provisions related to benefits for professionals entering for the first time in the job market, PF support being given by government to the employers are very positive initiatives and they are going to have a positive impact on us in the near future.

items.statement: Singapore Henderson business annualized revenue ~$40M, winning new contracts, turning profitable
items.quote: Singapore business, like I said, is back on feet, the business is now clocking close to $40 million in annualized revenue. It's winning new contracts, and I think it is on the angle of turning profitable, reasonably profitable if things go to plan.

items.statement: VProtect investments long gestation, high double-digit returns, over 25,000 installations
items.quote: VProtect investments are concerned, yes, these are long gestation businesses, they require investment. But returns are in high double-digit range, which is much better than the rest of the business.

items.statement: Top line growth guided at higher teens to 20% and VoNB margin at +/- 28% for FY25
items.quote: Our top line growth will be in higher teens to 20% and regarding the margin also, we will be in the same range of plus/ minus 28% kind of.

items.statement: VoNB margin at 26.8% for Q1 FY25, down from previous period due to lower protection growth and not passing on rate drop
items.quote: VoNB Margin stands at 26.8% for the period ended June '24. The shift in VoNB is mainly on account of increase in share of ULIP business as compared to previous period and for a specific period in non-PAR savings, the impact of yield movement was absorbed by the Company instead of being passed on to the customers.

items.statement: Did not pass on interest rate drop to customers in non-PAR savings, absorbing impact on margins
items.quote: for a specific period in non-PAR savings, the impact of yield movement was absorbed by the Company instead of being passed on to the customers.

items.statement: Surrender value regulatory changes expected to have minimal margin impact (<1%) due to higher-than-required surrender values and prudent assumptions
items.quote: We will not exactly quantify but this will be definitely much lesser than the 1% number that you quoted.

items.statement: OPEX ratio improved to 6.1% from 6.8% YoY; total cost ratio improved to 10.5% from 10.8% YoY
items.quote: OPEX ratio stands at 6.1% for the quarter ended June 30th, 2024, as compared to 6.8% for corresponding quarter of previous year. Our total cost ratio stands at 10.5% for the period ended June 30 th as compared to 10.8% for corresponding quarter of last year

items.statement: No commission structure changes planned for corporate or individual agents despite new IRDAI surrender value norms
items.quote: As of now we are not planning any commission structure change for our corporate agents or for our individual agents and the rate structure will continue to be the same.

items.statement: 99% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 42% processed via automated underwriting
items.quote: With 99% of the individual proposals being submitted digitally. 42% of individual proposals are processed through automated underwriting.

items.statement: Appointed industry veteran as internal ombudsman, first in insurance industry, to strengthen customer grievance redressal
items.quote: we have created the position of internal ombudsman and appointed an industry veteran to set a new benchmark in customer satisfaction. This is first in the entire insurance industry.

items.statement: Agency channel IRP growth target ~43% for FY25; agency contribution to distribution mix slated to increase
items.quote: Agency almost grew by 43% on IRP basis. And that is the kind of growth we are looking for in t he current year so that our overall distribution m ix, the contribution of agency is slated to go up

items.statement: Loan book growth guidance of 18-20% and deposit growth higher than advances maintained
items.quote: Our stated strategy of growing secured book and a guidance of loan book growth of around 18 % to 20% and a deposit growth of higher than that will continue.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 7-7.5% range
items.quote: As guided before, we will continue to maintain our NIM in the range of 7% to 7.5 % depending on how the overall interest rate looks like.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 maintained at 1.8-2%
items.quote: However, for FY25, we continue to expect the credit cost to be in the range of 1.8% to 2% in line with our previous guidance, as we have seen some of the risks in the SMA-0 book that we've talked about.

items.statement: NIM at 7.6% in Q1FY25, up 22 bps YoY, protected despite cost of funds pressure
items.quote: Our net interest margin or NIM was 7.6% in Q1FY25, as compared to 7.3% in the same quarter previous year. It is important to note that despite some pressure on cost of funds, we have been able to sustain and protect our margins sequentially.

items.statement: Continued investment in people, technology and branches planned
items.quote: We would continue to invest in people, technology, and building key capabilities, as also mentioned by Ratan and Rajinder, in terms of driving the strategic growth targets that we have for the Bank.

items.statement: Focus on growing secured assets faster than microfinance to change portfolio mix
items.quote: Within the products , we are looking to Bandhan Bank July 26, 2024 improve the share of our secured assets portfolio And that will be the direction where we are trying to increase that w hich would mean that whil st the asset growth will happen both in the microfinance book as well as the secured book, the growth percentage for the secured book will be faster compared to the microfinance

items.statement: EEB portfolio risk weight increased from 75% to 125%, impacting CRAR by 362 bps
items.quote: This increase in risk weightage of our EEB portfolio has an impact of about 362 b ps on our overall capital adequacy ratio. Consequently, our CRAR stands at 15% and including profit of Q1FY25, it is at 15.7%.

items.statement: Q1 advances grew 1% QoQ reversing historical seasonal decline trend
items.quote: However, this year, instead of a decline, we have seen a 1% sequential growth in advances, so thereby reversing the trend that has been seen in the previous years.

items.statement: Yield on advances expected to be range-bound at 15-16% due to secured mix shift offset by lower slippages
items.quote: So, we do expect the yields to be between overall around 15 % to 16%, that kind of a range.

items.statement: Security receipt redemption expected to contribute Rs 60-70 crore quarterly for FY25
items.quote: We are expecting on a quarterly basis a range of Rs. 60 to Rs. 70 crores of steady numbers to come through on this particular line. So, I think that will continue to happen. I think your second part. Pramit Shah: How many quarters? Rajeev Mantri: At least for this year, for this financial year, we expect that number

items.statement: SMA-0 increased 30 bps QoQ to 0.9% due to heat waves and floods in some geographies
items.quote: However, in the SMA -0 book, we have seen an increase of 30 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 0.9% at the levels of Rs. 580 crores. And this is primarily on account of some slowdown in collections due to the heat wave and floods that we have seen in certain geographical areas within the country.

items.statement: Punjab and Maharashtra showing stress in microfinance portfolio recently
items.quote: In the last quarter the stress is coming from Punjab and Maharashtra primarily though there have been talks of Bihar as well, but Bihar has been doing well across thus far. But definitely Punjab and Maharashtra are two states which are giving little bit of a stress.

items.statement: Branch expansion to slow significantly after adding ~500 branches in last 18 months
items.quote: We mentioned that in the past that over the last 18 months we have added up to around 500 odd branches. Going forward, number of new additional branches will be much lesser.

items.statement: No capital raise needed currently; internal stress testing shows adequate capital for 3 years
items.quote: As of now, we don't feel the need for it.

items.statement: CGFMU audit nearing closure, management confident of positive outcome
items.quote: The audit process is nearing a closure. The management is confident of having a positive closure soon.

items.statement: Cost of funds pressure building in market, will calibrate deposit strategy accordingly
items.quote: But on question on the cost of funds, as we have seen, I think in the market, there is some pressure building on the cost of funds. So, we will continue to ensure that why is the focus on the deposits happen. We will have to be cognizant of the pressures on cost of funds building in the market and accordingly calibrate our strategy.

items.statement: Projecting additional 6 GW capacity for FY25, with majority solar and ~700 MW wind
items.quote: as we had guided, we are projecting additional 6 gigawatt capacity for this year, out of which we have just commissioned 250 megawatt wind, which will essentially become a backbone of our operations in Khavda. Going forward, majority of our operations are targeted towards, you know, solar in both Rajasthan and Khavda, but we're expecting close to 700 megawatt of additional wind capacity, which wil

items.statement: Committed to 50 GW capacity target by 2030 including at least 5 GW energy storage via pump hydro
items.quote: Adani Green is absolutely committed to achieve 2030 capacity target of 50 gigawatt, including at least 5 gigawatt of energy storage through pump hydro.

items.statement: Total capex for 50 GW target exceeds INR 240,000 crores (~$30 billion) including pumped storage
items.quote: If you look at the total capex, which will be in excess of INR 240,000 crores, which includes pumped storage as well. So, it's a big number, which we will continue to optimize and make sure that we get the most out of this thing. If you convert it into US dollars, it's closer to $30 billion.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 92.6% driven by tech-enabled O&M, expected to improve with AI/ML integration
items.quote: Our EBITDA from power supply increased by 23% to INR2,374 crores with an industry-leading EBITDA margin of 92.6%. This exceptional margin is driven by tech-enabled operations and maintenance, which are expected to improve further with integration of AI and ML.

items.statement: Current solar merchant realization ~INR 4/unit in Q1, expected to pick up to north of INR 4.5 in Q2-Q4
items.quote: the current realization for the year average until now is around INR 4. However, this particular period of Q1 has seen - last year and the year before as well - some softening in prices because of the way the market works, because more solar is available in that period. However, it will pick up as it picks up every year as we move forward in Q2 and Q3 and later in Q4. So, we expect a good realizat

items.statement: Fresh borrowings at 8.6-8.9%; refinancing below 8.6%; portfolio average borrowing cost to decline from 9.4%
items.quote: some of our fresh borrowings which we have recently done are at a level of less than 9%. What you can say is, it is between 8.6% to 8.9% which is what we are doing right now. Refinancing of our projects are at a level which is even lesser than 8.6%.

items.statement: C&I demand growing due to carbon efficiency regime, data centers, hard-to-abate sectors decarbonization
items.quote: Our respected Finance Minister talked about how she is going to introduce, efficiency and intensity based carbon regime. This is going to unlock a new sphere of business for C&I. And we being the single largest renewable energy provider, we will directly benefit with some of these trends in the market.

items.statement: ~10 GW PPAs signed to deliver; flexibility to mix merchant, C&I, RTC, FDRE, hybrid revenues
items.quote: As we stand here today, we have close to 10-gigawatt worth of PPAs already signed, which I am supposed to deliver. So, that flexibility is already there with me that I can execute those PPAs if I want to, as PPAs for the next two years, as I mix more and more merchant, C&I, and other types of revenues.

items.statement: No further equity raise needed; promoter warrants and internal cash flows to fund 50 GW growth
items.quote: No, I think as we had explained before, the promoter warrants money is expected and we are tapping into it as we need. So, we have that, already done. The way we have designed the project and the way our cash flows from existing projects work and the new projects will also throw in a lot of free cash flow. So, it will essentially help us make sure that we fund this growth, without any further equi

items.statement: Net debt to run-rate EBITDA ~4.0x; not expected to increase despite 6 GW addition in FY25
items.quote: you would have seen for my full year, net debt to run rate EBITDA is nearer to 4.0x. And the way my free cash flows will grow, as Amit was talking in the beginning, on the top of 10.9 gigawatt, I will be adding 6 gigawatt. And incrementally, the free cash flow will grow. We don't expect net debt to run-rate EBITDA to be of a level higher than what we have right now.

items.statement: CAPEX for FY25 is INR 201 Crore for two greenfield plants in Kothavadi and Bhiwadi
items.quote: CAPEX for FY '25 stands at INR 201 Crore. We are putting up two plants, one in Kothavadi and one in Bhiwadi.

items.statement: Kothavadi Phase-1 to complete within 12 months with trial production in Q4 FY25 and robust revenue from H2 FY26
items.quote: Even though we estimated 24 to 30 months for implementation, I think within 12 months we will be able to complete the Phase-1. We will be able to start some little trial production in Q4 and next year in th e second half, we will see a robust revenue coming in from that

items.statement: Bhiwadi Phase-1 to complete in 15 months with trial production in Q4 FY25, fully available next financial year
items.quote: We have said 18 to 24 months, but I think we will be able to complete the Phase-1 project in 15 months, and we are likely to start the trial production in Q4 of this year. So, this will be fully available for next financial year.

items.statement: DR Axion operations robust with additional orders won in India and for export
items.quote: We have won a little more orders, additional orders within India, also for export requirements. So, the operations are looking robust even going forward.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreement to acquire German foundry assets in Fronberg for EUR 5.5M plus EUR 0.5M debt, with INR 60 Crore additional investment planned
items.quote: We have signed a definitive agreement to acquire high technology foundry, the assets of high technology foundry in Germany in Fronberg and this has got marquee customers for the engine blocks for industrial engines.

items.statement: Aluminum margins optically 1-1.5% lower due to 12-13% commodity price inflation inflating top line
items.quote: Artificially, the top line is inflated by 12-13%. That is maybe the EBITDA optically looks 1% to 1.5% lower.

items.statement: M&HCV still declining, tractor showing green shoots end of Q1, two-wheeler robust, passenger vehicle slowed after strong growth
items.quote: M&HCV is still not showing any respite. It's still on a declining trend, whereas there have been green shoots in the tractor industry at the end of the 1st Quarter. Two-wheeler has been very robust. Passenger vehicle has slowed down after a good one-year growth period.

items.statement: Powertrain growth expected from FY27 onwards with industrial engine segment, FY26 Q4 initial revenue
items.quote: It will happen from FY '27 onwards. FY '26, from Q4 onwards it will start seeing, but after that we will see, I think, many years of good growth on the Powertrain, regardless of the commercial vehicle business.

items.statement: Export orders for passenger vehicle aluminum parts: two trial shipments done, third next week, production from Q4 FY25 targeting INR 125 Crore revenue next year
items.quote: We have done two trial shipments already completed. Third trial shipment is going next week and production is slated to start from Q4 onwards. Next year we are looking at an upward revenue of around INR 125 Crore from the export of this particular product to Korea.

items.statement: Management bandwidth addressed: DR Axion needs no new CAPEX or management, Fronberg self-contained with existing team, Sunbeam brings experienced management
items.quote: We are not going to put any management in Europe. We are not going to recruit any management in Europe. We may recruit somebody here on a visit basis, not even permanently putting up there.

items.statement: Aluminum commodity prices up 12-13% quarter-on-quarter, inflating top line optically
items.quote: Some market research shows that 15% of commodity prices have gone up even quarter-on-quarter. Some say, it is 12-13%. Let us take the lower number 12-13%.

items.statement: German foundry (Fronberg) revenue ~INR 250 Crore (EUR 25M) with high single-digit EBITDA, historically EBIT positive except crisis years
items.quote: Calendar year '21 was EUR 23 Million. So, we will just take a number of Rs. 100. So, to convert it was INR 232 Crore in '21 calendar year, '22 was INR 255 Crore and calendar year '23 was INR 257 Crore and calendar year '24, as I understand from the management, it is around a similar number. So, it's around INR 250 Crore is the top line. And they have been having high single-digit EBITDA.

items.statement: Consolidated aluminum capacity 60,000-70,000 tons, subscale vs global peers (INR 10,000-20,000 Crore), driving acquisition strategy
items.quote: Overall, when you look at the tonnage currently, we are having, it is close to around 60,000-70,000 tons. Depending on product mix, we are at that range currently.

items.statement: CAPEX guidance flexible, will increase if growth materializes, currently focused on two plants and acquisitions
items.quote: We see potential growth for next financial year to be much bigger. Then we may increase the CAPEX. But now with this acquisition, we are looking at how to distribute the cash flow and acquisition targets, how to ramp it up. So, it is a work in progress as of now.

items.statement: Expect 20% top-line growth in FY25 and FY26
items.quote: Similarly, this year also because the last year was a bottom year, we expect 20% top line growth in this financial year as well as next financial year.

items.statement: Targeting ~15% EBITDA margin on average in FY26
items.quote: And in the next financial year, we are targeting about 15% of EBITDA margin on an average.

items.statement: Agrochemical prices down ~25% YoY in Q1 FY25; expect QoQ improvement from Q2
items.quote: So in the Q1, the price reduction, particularly in the case of agrochemical, was drastically compared to the first quarter of last financial year. I would say it is in the range of about 25%.

items.statement: Interim antidumping duty on TiO2 from China expected in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We are also expecting interim antidumping duty on Titanium Dioxide from China probably in the Q3 of FY25.

items.statement: Plan to repay ~INR 173 cr debt in FY25 and similar in FY26; target substantial debt reduction in 2 years
items.quote: in the first -- in this financial year, we'll be repaying about close to INR 173 crore of loan repayment, so which will bring us to quite reasonable level. Similarly, in the next financial year also, it will be close to same amount repayment will be there. So our target is to bring down the debt level substantially low in next 2 years

items.statement: Expect return to profitability from Q2 FY25 after 4-5 quarters of losses
items.quote: From the Q2 onwards, there are very good chance we'll be in profitability, and we are committed for the same for the growth point of view as well as profitability point of view.

name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd

items.statement: Opex guidance: employee cost 10-12%, other Opex 10-12%
items.quote: So, the expenses, mainly we have been generally projecting that the expenses will grow in the inflation plus something. So maybe the cost of employees will be in the range of around 10%-12%. Other than that, other Opex will grow in the range of around 10% -12%, which is the administrative Opex.

items.statement: ESOP cost around Rs 3 crore per quarter
items.quote: So Dipanjan, the ESOP cost is in the range of around ₹3-odd crores which is already a part of the employee benefit cost.

items.statement: Equity yield 68 bps; new fund yield lower due to 65% DTR sharing
items.quote: On yield, equity is in the range of around 68 bps. And new, generally, depending on a scheme to scheme, but we generally share around 65% of our DTR with the distributors. So, the yield on the new will be lower than the overall yield on the old stock.

items.statement: Debt yield 25-26 bps; liquid yield 12-13 bps
items.quote: Debt is in the range of around 25-26 basis and liquid is in the range of around 12-13 basis.

items.statement: SIP book Rs 1,367 crore in June 2024, up 39% YoY; quarterly SIP flows ~Rs 3,700 crore
items.quote: SIP numbers during the quarter further moved up to cross ed ₹1,300 crores mark, showing a 39% year -on-year increase, from ₹987 crores in June 2023 to ₹1,367 crores in June 2024.

items.statement: SIP AUM Rs 77,000 crore as of June 2024
items.quote: It is ₹77,000 crore Lalit.

items.statement: Passive AUM ~Rs 29,900 crore, 7.53 lakh folios, 44 products; hired Head of Passives
items.quote: On the passive front, as of June 2024, our passive assets total approximately ₹29,900 crores. Our customer base has grown to about 7.5 3 lakh folios and have a diverse product portfolio of about 44 products.

items.statement: Alternative segment focus: PMS/AIF, Category II/III AIFs, GIFT City funds, ABSL Global Emerging Market Fund near Rs 400 crore
items.quote: We have launched and are currently under a fundraising plan for funds for ABSL Global Emerging Market Fund which invests in emerging markets. We have already touched the size of close to about ₹400 crores.

items.statement: NFO pipeline: Innovation Fund approved, Defence Index Fund approved, more board-approved products to be filed with SEBI
items.quote: We already have 2 approvals. One approved we already have, is the Innovation Fund approval that we already have. We have one fund approval for a defence fund on the index side which we intend to launch very soon.

items.statement: Capital gains tax hike not expected to dampen equity flows; fixed income status quo; REITs/InvITs/gold now attract equity taxation
items.quote: The increase in capital gain taxes may not dampen my belief is market sentiment or also have significant negative impact more than the market on the mutual fund industry.

items.statement: Highest-ever quarterly profit: revenue Rs 481 crore (+24% YoY), PAT Rs 232 crore (+26% YoY)
items.quote: Our total revenue is about ₹481 crores vs ₹389 crores in Q1 of FY24, up 24% Y-o-Y. Our profit after tax is at ₹232 crores vs ₹185 crores in Q1 FY24 up 26% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Overall QAAUM Rs 3.68 lakh crore (+19% YoY); MF QAAUM Rs 3.53 lakh crore; Equity QAAUM Rs 1.62 lakh crore
items.quote: Overall Average Assets under Management including alternate assets, reached ₹3.68 lakh crores, reflecting a 19% year-on-year growth. Our Mutual Fund Quarterly Average AUM reached ₹3.53 lakh crores, with Equity quarterly average AUM about ₹1.62 lakh crores.

items.statement: Added 8.39 lakh new SIPs (3x YoY); 9 lakh new folios (total 94 lakh); folio growth 9% vs industry 7%
items.quote: We added around 8.39 lakh new SIPs, mainly we have seen a 3x increase from the previous year. We have witnessed healthy growth in our investor's folio. Have added around 9 lakh new folios during the quarter bringing our total serviced folios to 94 lakhs.

items.statement: Quant Fund NFO collected ~Rs 2,400 crore, one of largest in category and highest collection in many years
items.quote: We had a successful NFO collection of Aditya Birla Sun Life Quant Fund mobilizing assets of around ₹2,400 crores. It is now one of the largest funds in this category. And for us, also, it was one of the highest collections we have had in the last so many numbers of years.

items.statement: GIFT City: Global Emerging Market Fund near close (~Rs 400 cr, 40-50 bps yield); Global Blue-chip Fund approved for LRS/ODI; ESG Engagement Fund seed capital coming, launch next quarter
items.quote: that already started is coming to a closure by September end, where we already done about ₹400 crores from the LRS side. That fund will give me about 40 to 50 basis points of additional revenue

items.statement: Target 120-150 net store additions for FY25
items.quote: We are optimistic about our continued store expansion efforts and aim to open between 120 and 150 stores for full year FY'25.

items.statement: Target 19-20% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin for FY25
items.quote: So moving forward for the full year, we would ideally want to be in the range of 19% to 20% pre Ind AS EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Target 4-5% SSSG by end of FY25
items.quote: Our idea is to at least by the end of the year reach to that number. Our target is that. We are working very hard to get to that number.

items.statement: Target EBO sales growth >15% YoY with 4-5% SSSG
items.quote: My target internally is to go the EBO network more than 15%. The EBO sales on a Y-o-Y basis with an SSSG push of about 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Advertising spend to remain at 2% of revenue for FY25
items.quote: It's going to be at 2%. It's not going to cross 2%.

items.statement: Inventory days to stabilize at 90-95 days for FY25
items.quote: For the full year, we expect this to be in the range of 90 to 95 days.

items.statement: First Middle East store to open in FY25 under FOFO model with Apparel Group
items.quote: Lastly, our tie up with Apparel Group in the Middle East is on track, and we should open our first door in this financial year.

items.statement: Annual capex of ~INR50 crores for 120-130 store additions funded by internal accruals
items.quote: We typically require about INR50 crores of annual investment in our business for adding 120 to 130 stores, which should very well be taken care by our internal accruals itself.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 50 bps YoY in Q1 FY25; expect further improvement in coming quarters
items.quote: As far as gross margins are concerned, we have seen a 50 bps increase in gross margin. So we would probably see a little more improvement in the coming quarters as far as GM is concerned.

items.statement: Pledge release targeted between August and December 2024
items.quote: We are looking to clear the pledge between the window of August and December. So most of the pledge should get released between this window.

items.statement: Repeat purchase rate stable at 40-45%; new activewear collection targeting Gen Z showing good traction
items.quote: our repeat purchase has actually not really changed much. It's at around 40% to 45%. But very rightly you pointed out, even this this quarter, we had actually launched our activewear collection in our bottom wear category. And we have seen very good traction

items.statement: LFS channel growth of ~40% in Q1 FY25 to normalize in Q2 due to one-time partner promotion
items.quote: This will normalize, Devanshu. So you would see the contribution coming down. This was a very unique quarter because one of our LFS partners had actually had an offer running in their store.

items.statement: Store closures expected at 6-7 for full year FY25
items.quote: I think for the full year, it will be in low single digits. It will be in single digits. It might be around 6 to 7 closed for the full year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR 2,600-2,700 crores implying 15-19% growth
items.quote: To summarize at the close, we are reasonably confident of achieving our FY'25 revenue guidance of INR 2,600 crores to INR 2,700 crores, which would translate into a growth of 15% to 19% for the year.

items.statement: FY25 capex guided at INR 300 crores
items.quote: We have guided to a INR 300 crores for this year. We said we do INR 200 crores average over a block of two to three years because last year's capex was INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Q1 order book wins in Managed Services and Technology Solutions at INR 200 crores
items.quote: In our Managed Service and Technology Solutions business, our order book wins for the quarter were fairly robust at INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Total order book roughly INR 2,000 crores including Q1 wins
items.quote: Kunal Sharma: And last one more thing. As far as the capex, sorry, the order book is concerned, roughly we have nearly including quarter 1 order book, roughly INR 2,000-odd crores order book, right? Rajiv Kaul: Yes.

items.statement: Adjusted PAT margin at 16.4% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Adjusted PAT has grown by 13% to INR 98.5 crores and adjusted PAT margin stood at 16.4%.

items.statement: Managed Services EBIT margin at 17% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The EBIT in this segment has grown 20% year-on-year to INR 41 crores, and the EBIT margin stood at 17%.

items.statement: Consumption subdued in Q1 but expected to improve in Q2 and Q3 with festive season
items.quote: Consumption was slightly subdued in Q1, which seems to be a cross-sector theme, but we expect it to improve in Q2 and Q3 with the festive season.

items.statement: Managed Services revenue mix at 39% end FY24, targeting 40% range (+/-2-3%) for FY25
items.quote: We had expected to reach 40% revenue contribution from MS and Tech by FY'25. FY'24 end, we are at 39%. We think we'll be at the 40% range now, plus or minus 2%-3%.

items.statement: Risk cost (bad debt provisions) around 4% for FY24, targeting 4-4.5% range going forward
items.quote: Rajiv Kaul: Roughly about 4%.

items.statement: BLA business capped at 15% of overall revenue, currently at ~13%
items.quote: We've also stated that, as a policy, we have given a direction that we will cap our BLA oriented businesses at 15% of our overall revenue.

items.statement: ATM interchange hike awaited; could drive ATM growth and higher outsourcing if approved
items.quote: There also has been a fair amount of discussion on the ATM interchange hike for both bank-owned ATMs as well as white label ATMs, and we await a positive policy decision in the coming months.

items.statement: Majority of FY24 order book execution expected to go live in next two quarters
items.quote: As Pankaj I think talked about, the fact that the majority of the orders we won in last year should go live in the next two quarters, majority.

items.statement: Capex primarily growth-oriented for executing new wins including technology projects
items.quote: I think a large part of this capex will be growth capex and a very little -- lesser portion would be on maintenance.

items.statement: FY27 guidance expected by end of FY25 or second half of FY25
items.quote: As soon as we feel reasonably confident of the guidance we will come back to you. But I would say, in the second half of the year or the end of FY'25, we owe you an FY'27 guidance.

items.statement: Expect 1,000-2,000 ATM additions in BLA on transaction-linked model
items.quote: I would think that we in our mind think about 1,000-2,000 ATMs addition in BLA on the transaction-linked model.

items.statement: Near-term objective is to grow and scale digital business by building open-loop PPI infrastructure through issuance of cards and wallets; continue strengthening ATM outsourcing, cash business, and focus on increasing revenue share from serv
items.quote: Our near-term objective is to grow and scale the digital business by building an open-loop PPI infrastructure through the issuance of cards and wallets. We will continue to strengthen our ATM outsourcing business, our cash business, and focus on increasing revenue share from our services.

items.statement: Renewed contract with leading private sector bank under hybrid model generating additional annual revenue of INR300 million
items.quote: This contract allows a hybrid model which covers a fixed fee and a transaction fee. It will generate additional annual revenue of INR300 million while maintaining the existing cost structure thus improving profitability and margins.

items.statement: SBI deployment of 1,350 ATMs generating one-time revenue of INR750 million on track for completion by H1 FY25
items.quote: the deployment of 1,350 ATMs which will generate a one-time revenue of INR750 million is on track and will be completed by H1 of this financial year.

items.statement: New SBI order of 2,500+ ATMs under outsourcing portfolio starting H2 FY25, order value INR11,000 million over seven years adding INR1,500 million annual revenue
items.quote: Another order win of 2,500 plus ATMs under outsourcing portfolio will begin in the second half of this financial year and is expected to complete by this financial year. The order value is around INR11,000 million over seven years which will add INR1,500 million on an annual basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 29.9% vs 27.1% in Q1 FY24; absolute EBITDA INR1,053 million vs INR1,030 million in Q1 FY24
items.quote: in Q1 of FY25, the EBITDA margin stood at 29.9% versus 27.1% in Q1 of FY24. Our EBITDA on absolute terms stood at INR1,053 million in of FY25 versus INR934 million in Q4 of FY24 and INR1,030 million in Q1 of FY24

items.statement: Indian ATM industry projected to grow at 9.2% CAGR 2024-2032; RFPs for 18,000-20,000 ATMs/CRMs underway in H1
items.quote: The Indian ATM industry is projected to grow at a CAGR of 9.2% between 2024 to 2032. This is due to the growing demand for ATMs and CRMss. As leading banks expand their branches, various RFPs in the range of 18,000 to 20,000 ATMs and CRMs are currently underway in the first half.

items.statement: Pilot of Ongo fueling near completion, expect launch in H1 FY25; onboarded ~1,300 fleet vehicles; testing AI-enabled voice-controlled fueling
items.quote: I am happy to inform you that the pilot of Ongo fueling which will be our flagship product under digital business is near to completion and we expect to launch it in H1 of FY25. We have onboarded close to 1300 fleet vehicles in this phase. For added convenience of the consumers, we are testing AI enabled voice-controlled fueling on the same platform.

items.statement: Set up new cash vault facility of 14,000 sq ft in Bengaluru, Karnataka for world-class cash processing and vault services
items.quote: During the recently concluded quarter, we have set up a new cash vault facility spread over an area of 14,000 square feet in Bengaluru, Karnataka. This state-of-the-art facility will offer world-class cash processing and vault services.

items.statement: Initiated equity fundraise of INR2,000 million (INR200 crores) through preferential allotment for sustainable long-term growth
items.quote: Lastly, I would like to share that the company has initiated an equity fundraise of INR2,000 million i.e. INR200 crores through preferential allotment. This will help us drive sustainable growth for our business in the long term.

items.statement: Plan to become debt-free over next 3-4 years; term loans being consistently reduced; preferential allotment proceeds partly for debt repayment, working capital, and general corporate purposes
items.quote: And I think the plan of the company is to definitely become debt free over a period of time in the next three to four years as we have already communicated last time also. And the money that we are collecting is definitely going to get used for the business purpose, expansion purpose and maybe for working capital purpose also as per the defined end use that we have given in our offer letter also

items.statement: Volume growth target of 13% to 15% for the company
items.quote: So volume growth, what we are targeting that we want to grow volume at between 13% to 15%. That's the target what we are taking on at the company.

items.statement: Gross margin target maintained at 32% despite commodity inflation
items.quote: So there's a target what we've taken that we need to maintain 32% in gross margin level. Because ultimately, as a brand is growing, we are focusing more on branding, more on brand equity, working more on distribution.

items.statement: Price increase of 1.5% expected for the year, with 2-3% over 7-8 months
items.quote: So the 2% to 3% would remain for seven, eight months largely. So yearly, we'll see 1.5%.

items.statement: Major capex completed; only minimal maintenance and NPD capex going forward
items.quote: On capex plan, we completed most of the capex. So in coming years, there will be minimal capex that will be just NPDs or regular maintenance capex. We'll not see any major capex in the coming years.

items.statement: Export growth target of 20%-25% for the year
items.quote: We are targeting 20%-25% growth in export. That's what we are targeting.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 13.7% excluding PLI income in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So without PLI also, the EBITDA is closed to 13.7%. So if we exclude PLI income, the EBITDA is 13.7% from gross margin lens also.

items.statement: Commodity inflation seen in chana, pulses, dry fruits, and potato; price hikes of 0.7-0.8% taken in Q1
items.quote: We've done some price hikes compared to last quarter within close to 0.7%, 0.8% price hike on average level on the company.

items.statement: Rural demand recovery continuing; monsoon and budget expected to support growth
items.quote: And quarter one, if you look at has continued in that trend, so we see quite a recovery in the rural sector as well. With the kind of budget which has come in and the money getting infused into rural and in job creation opportunity, we strongly believe that this momentum should continue.

items.statement: Family packs grew 17.3% and contribute 56.7% of business; impulse packs at 42.8%
items.quote: Our family pack grew at 17.3% and impulse was relatively low. So the point is that the momentum on the family pack continues, and that's the growth that we have delivered. And hence, coming on to our contribution of family packs stays at 56.7%, and the impulse is 42.8% to our overall business.

items.statement: Direct distribution target of 50,000 outlets per year; aim for 350,000 direct outlets by end of next year
items.quote: Just from direct reach, we would want to add 50,000 in each year. So we think that by end of next year, it should be at about 350,000 outlets, directly covered.

items.statement: Focus states market share target of mid-single digits (4.5%) in three years from current 1.8%
items.quote: what we believe that some will do much, much better, some may not do as much good, but we are looking at that we should be reasonably mid-single digits kind of a market share is what we should reach. And within this, you will see certain states above that high-single and some would be little below that. So that's the number. Percy: Right. Manoj Verma: So, to sum it up, it is almost doubling this n

items.statement: A&P spend targeted at 1.75% of revenue for full year; higher in Q2 and Q3
items.quote: At an average, we'll be targeting 1.75% of overall ads spend. That's what we are thinking.

items.statement: Staff cost target at 5.5%-5.7% of revenue; current run rate includes ESOP and reclassification
items.quote: But overall, when we see a percentage level, so our target should take around 5.5%, close to 5.7%.

items.statement: Expect to meet and exceed revenue estimate of INR30,000 million and EBITDA margin targeting 15% for FY25
items.quote: For the financial year 2025 going ahead, we expect to have a good traction from all the different verticals, and we will meet and exceed our estimates of 30,000 million of revenue and corresponding EBITDA margin targeting at 15% for FY '25.

items.statement: Order book surged from INR41,152 million in Q4 FY24 to INR50,386 million in Q1 FY25, a 22% sequential increase
items.quote: Our order book surged from INR41,152 million in quarter 4 FY '24 to INR50,386 million in quarter 1 FY '25.

items.statement: OSAT capex about INR3,000 crores by FY30; PCB capex expected INR1,200-1,400 crores by FY30
items.quote: our OSAT capex is about INR3,000 crores. So by FY’30, we can expect ab out INR3,500 crores revenues in this

items.statement: Box Build share expected to increase by end of FY25, especially in industrial and medical; exports to rise from 15% to 20-25% by FY26
items.quote: by end of year you will have Box Build share going up and rightly as rightly pointed out it drives also the margins a little higher.

items.statement: Strong demand across all verticals, notably industrial, EV, aerospace, outer space, strategic electronics, and railway; multi-year contracts with 4-6 year visibility
items.quote: Growth in order book is le d by strong demand across all verticals, more notably industrial and EV, aerospace, outer spa ce, and strategic electronics, along with railway segment

items.statement: Q1 margin pressure due to election quarter impact on government offtake and product mix; working capital at 121 days due to inventory build for planned execution and receivable delays
items.quote: in the first quarter if you notice it is almost an election quarter actually. And we are glad that we got to where we actually reached.

items.statement: Telangana facility first phase to be operational by end of August 2024; Gujarat land acquired for OSAT, construction starting shortly; HDI PCB project proceeding as per plan
items.quote: Telangana facility first phase will be up and running by the end of August 2024.

items.statement: Net working capital average for FY25 expected to be superior to last year's 83 days, targeting 70s by year-end
items.quote: I am quite confident by end of this year; we will reach better th an what it was last year. And as we’ve been indicating, it will be in 70s

items.statement: Consolidated $1 billion revenue target by FY28 including OSAT and PCB; 70-75% from EMS, remainder from new businesses
items.quote: $1 billion is our aspirational target as of FY'28, sir. And like I said, I was explaining the 75% to 80% will be our existing EMS business.

items.statement: OSAT revenues expected to start in Q4 FY26 with reasonable capacity utilization; PCB revenues expected in FY26
items.quote: we certainly will have a reasonable and reasonably significant capacity utilization and revenues.

items.statement: Kavach R&D investment of INR40 crores; proof of concept by Q1 FY26; three business models possible including direct supply and OEM manufacturing
items.quote: we will be investing around INR40 crores of in R&D investment into this project. Proof of conce pt is what we are being done now and this should be in the market by the first quarter of 2026

items.statement: Smart meter opportunity: 240 million meters remaining from 250 million target; price range INR2,000-5,000 per meter; 5-10 year business horizon
items.quote: another 240 million meters at the minimum will be there. Then of course, we are also -- it's a similar technology.

items.statement: OSAT and PCB businesses expected to be margin accretive vs EMS; OSAT targeting 25% legacy assembly, 75% advanced packaging
items.quote: all I can tell you at this point in time is it will be marg in accretive to the existing

items.statement: OSAT subsidies: central government 50% pari-passu, state government 20-25% contingent on operations commencement; land at 50% discount
items.quote: central government gives us 50% subsidy. That 50% subsidy is issued on a pari-passu basis.

items.statement: Medical equipment: qualified by one of world's leading providers in Europe and US; expect business ramp-up from this large customer
items.quote: one of the world’s leading medi cal equipment providers has qualified us both in Europe as well as in the US business
